```csharp
//                  two surfaces, so a scene CHANGE reads as intent
//
// Stagger spreads a group over time, Easings gives the curve. EaseOutBack
// overshoots slightly, which is what makes something "pop" instead of "appear".

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

// Segments are declared once, outside the scene.
var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.4)
    .Add("bars", 2.0)
    .Add("word", 1.8)
    .Add("swap", 1.6);

var palettes = new (Color A, Color B)[]
{
    (Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.85, 0.95), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.30, 0.75)),
    (Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.72, 0.20), Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.20, 0.10)),
    (Color.FromRgb(0.65, 0.95, 0.30), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.45, 0.25)),
};

// Update() returns true exactly when the pick changed - the moment to re-bake
// anything that depends on the variant.
var picker = new CyclePicker(palettes.Length);

// Two pictures to transition between.
var pageA = new RasterSurface(24, 24);
var pageB = new RasterSurface(24, 24);

var letters = new[] { "P", "X", "L" };

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    picker.Update(cue.Cycle);
    var pal = palettes[picker.Current];

    ctx.DrawBackground(Colors.Black);

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "bars":
        {
            // Stagger.Progress: item i starts delayPerItem seconds after item i-1.
            for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++)
            {
                var u = Stagger.Progress(i, cue.LocalSeconds, duration: 0.5, delayPerItem: 0.12);
                var h = Easings.EaseOutBack(u) * (5 + i % 3 * 4);
                if (h <= 0) continue;
                ctx.DrawRectXyWh(1 + i * 4, 22 - h, 3, h,
                    colorFill: ColorOps.Lerp(pal.A, pal.B, i / 5.0), isAntialias: false);
            }
            break;
        }

        case "word":
        {
            // Spread ends the whole group at the same moment, whatever the count.
            for (var i = 0; i < letters.Length; i++)
            {
                var u = Stagger.Spread(i, letters.Length, cue.LocalSeconds, cue.Duration * 0.7, overlap: 0.5);
                if (u <= 0) continue;
                var e = Easings.EaseOutBack(u);
                var flash = MathH.Clamp01(1.0 - u * 1.8);
                ctx.DrawTextMono6x6(letters[i], 2 + i * 7, 9 + (1.0 - e) * 5.0,
                    color: ColorOps.Lerp(pal.A, Colors.White, flash).WithAlpha(MathH.Clamp01(u * 2.5)));
            }
            break;
        }

        case "swap":
        {
            // Prepare both pictures, then let the transition mix them.
            PaintPage(pageA, pal.A, pal.B);
            PaintPage(pageB, pal.B, pal.A);
            var u = cue.Progress;
            // Pick per cycle which transition is used - same code, different feel.
            switch (picker.Current)
            {
                case 0: Transitions.Wipe(ctx, pageA, pageB, u, angleDegrees: 20, softness: 2); break;
                case 1: Transitions.Iris(ctx, pageA, pageB, u, softness: 1.5); break;
                default: Transitions.Dissolve(ctx, pageA, pageB, u); break;
            }
            break;
        }
    }

    // Act name and a progress bar - useful while building, and a good habit:
    // if you cannot see the timeline, you cannot tune it.
    ctx.DrawTextCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.4));
    ctx.DrawRectXyWh(0, 23, 24 * cue.Progress, 1, colorFill: pal.A.WithAlpha(0.7), isAntialias: false);

    // SeamFade is 1 in the middle and ramps to 0 at both ends of the cycle.
    if (cue.SeamFade < 0.999)
        ctx.Filter(Filters.Fade(Colors.Black, 1.0 - cue.SeamFade));
};

void PaintPage(RasterSurface s, Color a, Color b)
{
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        s[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(a, b, (x + y) / 46.0);
    s.DrawCircle(12, 12, 6, colorStroke: Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.8), strokeWidth: 1);
}
```

### 16-day-night-and-light

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo16DayNightLight
// displayName: Day, Night and Light
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: One time-of-day value drives sky, sun and moon, ambient light, water and the light path
// ---

// INTENT: A day/night scene has exactly ONE source of truth - the DayCycle.
// Everything else is derived from it. But deriving it is only half the job; the
// other half is HOW the sky is painted, and that is where most attempts stay
// flat. Three things make the difference:
//
//   1. THREE horizon colours, not one. SkyGradient mixes a warm colour toward
//      the sun's column, a cool one toward the moon's, and a far colour
//      everywhere else. A single horizon colour gives an even orange wash; the
//      pull gives a warm COLUMN with cool sky beside it - that contrast IS the
//      sunset.
//   2. The body is stretched and layered. SkyGlow draws a halo, a glow and a
//      core, and squashes the ellipse sideways as the body sinks. A round disc
//      reads as a lamp, a smeared one as light through kilometres of air.
//   3. The glow OUTLIVES the core. The disc is cut at the horizon while the
//      glow keeps burning below it - that split is what an afterglow is.
//
// And then the water does it again: the same horizon colour continues below the
// line, and a SpecularBeam turns the reflection into a path of broken light.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const double horizonY = 13.0;

// Set to 0 to run on the real wall clock instead of fast-forwarding.
const double secondsPerDay = 30.0;

// The whole colour world of the scene, in one object.
var sky = new SkyGradient
{
    HorizonY = horizonY,
    PullSpread = 46.0,
    Top = new PhasePalette(
        night: Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.10),
        twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.18, 0.42),
        day: Color.FromRgb(0.38, 0.68, 1.00)),
    Horizon = new PhasePalette(
        night: Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.05, 0.14),
        twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.18, 0.10, 0.30),
        day: Color.FromRgb(0.92, 0.97, 1.00)),
    SunHorizon = new PhasePalette(
        night: Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.12, 0.20),
        twilight: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.22),
        day: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 1.00, 0.98)),
    MoonHorizon = new PhasePalette(
        night: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.38, 0.55),
        twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.42, 0.62),
        day: Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.98, 1.00)),
};

// The sun climbs high and narrow, the moon runs a low, wide arc that hugs the
// water - that is what puts its reflection into the frame.
var sun = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = horizonY, AmpX = 8, AmpY = 13 };
var moon = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = horizonY, AmpX = 13, AmpY = 6, PhaseOffset = Math.PI };

var sunGlow = SkyGlow.Sun();
var moonGlow = SkyGlow.Moon();

var stars = new StarField { Density = 0.05, TwinkleSpeed = 0.8 };
var sea = new WaveField { OriginY = horizonY, Octaves = 3, Speed = 1.3, CrossStrength = 0.35, DomainWarp = 0.45, PerspectiveSquash = 0.02 };
var beam = new SpecularBeam { TopY = horizonY, Length = 10, WidthBase = 0.8, WidthGrow = 0.55 };

var waterDeep = new PhasePalette(
    night: Color.FromRgb(0.01, 0.02, 0.06),
    twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.03, 0.15),
    day: Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.22, 0.50));

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cycle = secondsPerDay > 0 ? DayCycle.Animated(ctx, secondsPerDay) : DayCycle.FromClock(ctx);

    var s = sun.At(cycle);
    var m = moon.At(cycle);

    // Ambient light comes from the SUN only - moonlight is far too weak to give
    // objects their own colour back, which is why night is silhouettes.
    var light = Lighting.FromAltitude(s.Altitude, startAltitude: -3.0, fullAltitude: 9.0);

    // 1) SKY - one call, both bodies pulling their colour into the horizon.
    sky.Draw(ctx, cycle, s, m);

    // 2) STARS, before the bodies so a bright glow covers them.
    stars.Draw(ctx, t, visibility: cycle.Night, maxY: (int)horizonY);

    // 3) THE BODIES - stretched, layered, glow outliving the core.
    moonGlow.ShadowOffset = Moon.ShadowOffset(ctx.Now.ToUniversalTime()) * 3.2;
    moonGlow.Draw(ctx, m, maxY: horizonY, brightness: 0.85);
    sunGlow.Draw(ctx, s, maxY: horizonY);

    // 4) WATER - the horizon colour CONTINUES below the line, so the warm column
    //    does not stop at the horizon. Then the wave field lifts it per pixel.
    var deep = waterDeep.Sample(cycle);
    for (var y = (int)horizonY; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var depth = (y - horizonY) / (24.0 - horizonY);
        var top = sky.HorizonColorAt(x + 0.5, cycle, s, m);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(top, deep, Math.Sqrt(depth));
        var lift = sea.Value(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, t) * 0.09 * (0.4 + depth * 0.6);
        ctx[x, y] = new Color(MathH.Clamp01(c.R + lift), MathH.Clamp01(c.G + lift), MathH.Clamp01(c.B + lift));
    }

    // 5) THE LIGHT PATH - the strongest single element of a sunset over water.
    //    Three layers: a base beam, a glow on rising water, sparks on the crests.
    if (s.Fade(4.0) > 0.01)
    {
        beam.SourceX = s.X;
        beam.Draw(ctx, sea, t,
            beamColor: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.72, 0.35),
            glowColor: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.55),
            sparkColor: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.98, 0.90),
            intensity: s.Fade(4.0));
    }
    if (m.IsUp && cycle.Night > 0.1)
    {
        beam.SourceX = m.X;
        beam.Draw(ctx, sea, t,
            beamColor: Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.65, 0.90),
            glowColor: Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.82, 1.00),
            sparkColor: Colors.White,
            intensity: cycle.Night * 0.9);
    }

    // 6) FOAM on the crests, densest close to the viewer.
    for (var y = (int)horizonY + 1; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var depth = (y - horizonY) / (24.0 - horizonY);
        var crest = sea.Crest(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, t, 1.4, 0.7) * depth;
        if (crest <= 0.03 || !Scatter.Has(x, y, 0.45, 8.0)) continue;
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(ctx[x, y], sky.HorizonColorAt(x + 0.5, cycle, s, m), crest * 0.7);
    }

    // 7) AN ISLAND as a silhouette - lit by ambient only, so it turns black at
    //    dusk on its own. minAmbient keeps it just off pure black on the panel.
    //    The profile is a bump function, so it sits IN the water instead of
    //    ending in a wall.
    var island = light.Apply(Color.FromRgb(0.24, 0.32, 0.20), minAmbient: 0.10);
    var islandDark = light.Apply(Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.16, 0.11), minAmbient: 0.08);
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        // Two Gauss falloffs make the two-hump profile - no hand-typed exp.
        var hump = 4.2 * Falloff.Gauss(x - 4.5, 2.65)
                 + 1.4 * Falloff.Gauss(x - 8.0, 1.41);
        if (hump < 0.6) continue;
        var crest = horizonY - hump;
        for (var y = (int)Math.Round(crest); y <= (int)horizonY; y++)
            ctx.SetPixelSafe(x, y, y > horizonY - 1.5 ? islandDark : island);
    }

    // 8) The horizon line, sub-pixel accurate and following the swell.
    ctx.DrawRowLine(
        x => horizonY + sea.Value(x, horizonY, t) * 0.25,
        x => (sky.HorizonColorAt(x, cycle, s, m), 0.5 + 0.4 * cycle.Day));

    // The readout sits over the water, where the scene is darkest all day, and
    // stays small - the picture is the point, not the number.
    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(ctx.Now.ToString("HH:mm"), 18, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.7);
};
```

### 17-depth-ground-and-streaming

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo17DepthGroundStreaming
// displayName: Depth, Ground Plane and Streaming
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A pinhole camera, a perspective ground, objects streaming past, fog by distance
// ---

// INTENT: Depth on 24x24 is not 3D - it is four cheap tricks that agree with
// each other:
//   1. things further away are SMALLER          PinholeCamera.ScaleAt(wz)
//   2. and sit HIGHER on screen                 PinholeCamera.ProjectY(wz)
//   3. and lose CONTRAST                        Fog.Apply(...)
//   4. and are drawn FIRST                      Depth.BackToFront(...)
//
// Two tools, pick by what you have:
//   PinholeCamera  - you have world coordinates (wx = sideways, wz = distance)
//   GroundPlane    - you only have screen rows and want a plane that converges
//                    to a vanishing point (roads, rails, furrows, tiles)
//
// WorldStream moves objects past the camera and recycles them off-screen, with
// an edge fade so the recycling is never visible.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const double horizonY = 9.0;

var camera = new PinholeCamera { Height = 1.6, Focal = 24.0, HorizonY = horizonY, CenterX = 12.0 };
var stream = new WorldStream { Speed = 2.2, RecycleFrom = -26, RecycleTo = 26, FadeMarginPx = 10 };
var ground = new GroundPlane { HorizonY = horizonY, NearY = 24.0, VanishX = 12.0 };

// wx0 = where an object starts sideways, wz = how far away it stays.
var posts = new (double Wx0, double Wz)[]
{
    (-22, 18.0), (-11, 9.0), (0, 13.0), (11, 6.5), (22, 11.0),
};

var skyHaze = Color.FromRgb(0.82, 0.90, 1.00);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    // Sky
    for (var y = 0; y < (int)horizonY; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.25, 0.45, 0.80), skyHaze, y / horizonY);

    // GROUND PLANE: every row below the horizon has a depth in [0,1]. A lane
    // narrows toward the vanishing point; cross lines scroll toward the viewer
    // and give the motion something to read against.
    for (var y = (int)horizonY; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var depth = ground.DepthAt(y + 0.5);
        var baseCol = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.42, 0.22), Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.28, 0.13), depth);
        var laneCenter = ground.LaneCenterAt(y + 0.5, nearX: 12.0);
        var laneHalf = ground.LaneHalfWidthAt(y + 0.5, nearHalfWidth: 7.0);
        var cross = ground.CrossLine(y + 0.5, spacing: 0.16, scroll: -t * 0.9, thickness: 0.30);

        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        {
            var c = baseCol;
            if (Math.Abs(x + 0.5 - laneCenter) <= laneHalf)
            {
                c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.34, 0.32, 0.34), Color.FromRgb(0.14, 0.13, 0.15), depth);
                if (cross > 0.4 && Math.Abs(x + 0.5 - laneCenter) < laneHalf * 0.25)
                    c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Colors.White, cross * 0.8);
            }
            // Far rows fade into the horizon colour - the whole trick of depth.
            ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(skyHaze, c, MathH.Clamp01(0.15 + depth * 1.6));
        }
    }

    // STREAMING OBJECTS: fixed depth, drifting sideways, drawn back to front.
    var placed = stream.Place(posts, camera, t);
    foreach (var it in Depth.BackToFront(placed))
    {
        if (it.Visibility <= 0.01) continue;

        // Size in world units x pixels-per-world-unit at that depth.
        var h = 2.2 * it.Scale;
        var w = Math.Max(1.0, 0.35 * it.Scale);
        var haze = Fog.Amount(it.Wz, nearZ: 5, farZ: 22, nearHaze: 0.05, farHaze: 0.75);

        var post = Fog.Apply(Color.FromRgb(0.42, 0.28, 0.16), haze, skyHaze);
        var lamp = Fog.Apply(Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.40), haze * 0.6, skyHaze);

        ctx.DrawRectXyWh(it.ScreenX - w / 2, it.ScreenY - h, w, h,
            colorFill: post.WithAlpha(it.Visibility), isAntialias: false);
        ctx.DrawCircle(it.ScreenX, it.ScreenY - h, Math.Max(0.8, 0.5 * it.Scale),
            colorFill: lamp.WithAlpha(it.Visibility));
    }

    // Horizon line last, sub-pixel accurate so it never jitters.
    ctx.DrawRowLine(_ => horizonY, skyHaze, 0.5);
};
```

### 18-fields-water-and-weather

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo18FieldsWaterWeather
// displayName: Fields, Water and Weather
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: One wave field drives water, foam, reflection and a light beam - plus rain, fog and stars as layers
// ---

// INTENT: A FIELD is a number you can sample anywhere: field.Value(x, y, t).
// That is more useful than it sounds, because ONE field can drive many things
// at once - the water colour, the foam on the crests, the distortion of a
// reflection, how a boat rolls. They then agree with each other for free, which
// is what makes a surface look like one material instead of several effects.
//
//   WaveField   travelling sine trains, warped and crossed  -> water, flags, fog
//   Noise       value / fbm / ridged noise as a number      -> texture, terrain
//   Scatter     deterministic per-pixel placement           -> stars, flecks
//
// Weather layers are stateless: every drop is derived from its index and the
// time, so nothing is stored and nothing drifts out of sync.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const double waterY = 13.0;

// Declared once, outside the scene.
var sea = new WaveField
{
    OriginY = waterY,
    Octaves = 3,
    CrossStrength = 0.4,      // a counter-running train breaks the 1D look
    DomainWarp = 0.45,        // bends the fronts so they are not straight lines
    PerspectiveSquash = 0.02, // rows compress toward the horizon
    Speed = 1.4,
};

var moonBeam = new SpecularBeam { TopY = waterY, Length = 10, WidthBase = 0.8, WidthGrow = 0.5 };
// A moonlit night: dim the weather to the scene, the factory defaults are daylight.
var rain = Weather.Rain(0.7);
rain.Color = Color.FromRgb(0.42, 0.55, 0.78);
rain.Alpha = 0.4;
// The rain lands ON the water, not past it: far drops stop at the horizon,
// near ones at the bottom edge, each with a brief impact blip.
rain.FloorFarY = waterY + 0.5;
rain.FloorNearY = 23.5;
rain.Splash = 2.5;
var fog = new FogBank { CenterY = waterY - 1.5, Thickness = 3.0, Density = 0.35, Speed = 0.8, Color = Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.62, 0.75) };
var stars = new StarField { Density = 0.05 };

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var moonX = 12.0 + Math.Sin(t * 0.12) * 5.0;

    // 1) SKY + stars
    for (var y = 0; y < (int)waterY; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.14), Color.FromRgb(0.14, 0.12, 0.28), y / waterY);
    stars.Draw(ctx, t, visibility: 1.0, maxY: (int)waterY);
    ctx.DrawCircle(moonX, 4.0, 2.1, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.93, 0.82));

    // 2) WATER: base gradient plus the field as a brightness modulation. The
    //    same field value decides the colour AND the foam - one sample, two uses.
    for (var y = (int)waterY; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var depth = (y - waterY) / (24.0 - waterY);
        var w = sea.Value(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, t);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.20, 0.38), Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.05, 0.14), Math.Sqrt(depth));
        var lift = w * 0.05;
        ctx[x, y] = new Color(MathH.Clamp01(c.R + lift), MathH.Clamp01(c.G + lift), MathH.Clamp01(c.B + lift));
    }

    // 3) MIRROR: fold everything above the water line down, shifted sideways by
    //    the SAME field. A reflection that ripples with the water it sits in.
    ctx.Filter(Filters.Mirror(
        atY: waterY, fade: 0.6,
        tint: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.45, 0.75), tintStrength: 0.35,
        distortion: sea, distortionStrength: 0.9, seconds: t));

    // 4) The light path: a cone of broken highlights, not a mirrored disc.
    moonBeam.SourceX = moonX;
    moonBeam.Draw(ctx, sea, t, Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.65, 0.90), Colors.White, intensity: 0.9);

    // 5) FOAM: crest strength is 0 below the threshold and rises with the peak.
    //    Scatter keeps it from looking like a solid line.
    for (var y = (int)waterY + 1; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var crest = sea.Crest(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, t, threshold: 1.25, range: 0.7);
        if (crest <= 0.05 || !Scatter.Has(x, y, 0.5, 8.0)) continue;
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(ctx[x, y], Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.90, 1.00), crest * 0.6);
    }

    // 6) WEATHER as layers in front of everything, back to front:
    //    fog sits on the water line, rain is closest to the viewer.
    fog.Draw(ctx, t);
    rain.Draw(ctx, t);
};
```

### 19-particles-trails-assembly

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo19ParticlesTrailsAssembly
// displayName: Particles, Trails and Assemblies
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A picture becomes a cloud becomes a picture, with sparks and a phosphor trail
// ---

// INTENT: Three different things people call "particles":
//
//   PixelAssembly  a FINISHED picture is harvested into pixels and flown into
//                  place (or let go again). Use it for logos, wordmarks, an
//                  object that materialises.
//   ParticleField  free particles with gravity and drag: sparks, embers, splash.
//   TrailBuffer    the previous frames, dimmed - motion trails, phosphor, light
//                  painting.
//
// IMPORTANT: the canvas is cleared before every frame, so a trail can NOT be
// made by "not clearing". You need a TrailBuffer, and it must live OUTSIDE the
// scene lambda - like every piece of state.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.3)
    .Add("gather", 1.6)
    .Add("hold", 2.0)
    .Add("release", 1.4);

// The finished picture, rendered once into an offscreen surface.
var artwork = new BakedSurface(24, 24);

// State: all three live outside the scene.
var sparks = new ParticleField { Gravity = 14.0, Drag = 0.8 };
var trail = new TrailBuffer(24, 24, decay: 0.82);
List<PixelTarget> targets = null;
PixelAssembly assembly = null;
Mask artworkMask = null;
var sparksFiredCycle = -1L;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    // Build the assembly once: bake the picture, harvest its pixels, decide
    // where each pixel comes from and when it starts.
    if (targets is null)
    {
        artwork.Ensure("logo", s =>
        {
            s.DrawTextCentered("PXL", 7, Fonts.Mono6x6, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.90, 1.00));
            s.DrawCircle(12, 12, 10.5, colorStroke: Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.75, 1.00), strokeWidth: 1, isAntialias: false);
        });
        targets = PixelTargets.From(artwork.Surface, alphaThreshold: 0.4);
        artworkMask = Mask.FromAlpha(artwork.Surface, 0.4);
        assembly = new PixelAssembly(targets)
        {
            Duration = 0.9,
            Spread = 11.0,
            Gravity = 10.0,
            FlightColor = Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.45),
            SourceOf = _ => (12.0, 25.0),                                   // all rise from below
            DelayOf = i => Scatter.Value(targets[i].X, targets[i].Y) * 0.5, // stable per-pixel delay
        };
    }

    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    // A slow noise wash fills every pixel - it IS the background.
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.02, 0.06), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.06, 0.18),
            Noise.Fbm(x * 0.12, y * 0.12, t * 0.15, 3));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "gather":
            assembly.Draw(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);
            break;

        case "hold":
            ctx.DrawSurface(artwork.Surface);
            // A glint sweep confined to the artwork by a Mask - glass, not a light beam.
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Glint(cue.Progress, angleDegrees: 30, width: 2.5, strength: 0.5,
                mask: artworkMask));
            if (sparksFiredCycle != cue.Cycle && cue.LocalSeconds > 0.15)
            {
                sparksFiredCycle = cue.Cycle;
                sparks.Burst(12, 12, count: 24, speed: 9.0, color: Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.9, 0.55), life: 0.9, spreadDegrees: 360);
            }
            break;

        case "release":
            assembly.DrawReverse(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);
            break;
    }

    // Free particles: step, then draw. Additive drawing makes them stack to white.
    sparks.Step(ctx);
    sparks.Draw(ctx, additive: true);

    // Trail: an orbiting dot painted INTO the buffer, the buffer drawn on top.
    trail.Decay();
    var a = t * 1.2;
    trail.Surface.PlotAA(12 + Math.Cos(a) * 9, 12 + Math.Sin(a) * 9, Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.35, 0.6));
    trail.Draw(ctx, BlendMode.Plus);

    if (cue.SeamFade < 0.999) ctx.Filter(Filters.Fade(Colors.Black, 1.0 - cue.SeamFade));
};
```

### 20-shapes-profiles-and-blobs

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo20ShapesProfilesBlobs
// displayName: Shapes - Profiles, Blobs, Limbs, Voxels
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Four ways to build an object that primitives alone cannot draw
// ---

// INTENT: Circles and rectangles run out fast. These four cover almost
// everything a scene actually needs:
//
//   ProfileShape       a body described by its half-width per ROW
//                      -> bottles, vases, rockets, towers, trunks
//   BlobField          overlapping ellipse lobes with an irregular outline
//                      -> canopies, clouds, bushes, smoke, foam
//   DrawTaperedLine    a stroke that narrows and is shaded across its width
//                      -> branches, cables, masts, smoke trails
//   FillSupersampled   any procedural shape, anti-aliased by 4x4 sampling
//                      -> rotated sprites, shapes with holes, hand-built forms
//   DrawVoxelSprite    cubes in oblique projection, self-occluding
//                      -> rocks, houses, isometric props
//
// The profile and the blob field are also QUERYABLE - Contains, EdgeFactor,
// InBand, Sample - so the same object can be filled, shaded, labelled and
// dissolved from one definition.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("body", 3.0)
    .Add("blob", 3.0)
    .Add("limb", 3.0)
    .Add("voxel", 3.0);

// A bottle: rows of (y, half-width). Between the rows it interpolates.
var bottle = new ProfileShape(centerX: 12, rows: new (double Y, double HalfWidth)[]
{
    (3, 1.6), (5, 1.8), (7, 1.4), (9, 3.6), (11, 5.4), (20, 5.4), (22, 4.6),
});
// The bottle's footprint as a Mask, built once - it confines the glint below.
var bottleMask = Mask.FromPredicate(24, 24, (x, y) => bottle.Contains(x + 0.5, y + 0.5) ? 1.0 : 0.0);

// A canopy: five lobes. Lumpiness makes the silhouette irregular.
var canopy = new BlobField(
    new Blob(12, 8, 5.5, 4.2),
    new Blob(7, 10, 4.0, 3.4),
    new Blob(17, 10, 4.0, 3.4),
    new Blob(10, 5, 3.4, 3.0),
    new Blob(15, 5, 3.4, 3.0))
{ Lumpiness = 0.22 };

var rock = new[]
{
    new Voxel(0, 0, 0, 0), new Voxel(1, 0, 0, 0), new Voxel(2, 0, 0, 0), new Voxel(3, 0, 0, 0),
    new Voxel(0, 0, 1, 0), new Voxel(1, 0, 1, 0), new Voxel(2, 0, 1, 0), new Voxel(3, 0, 1, 0),
    new Voxel(1, 1, 0, 0), new Voxel(2, 1, 0, 0), new Voxel(1, 1, 1, 1), new Voxel(2, 1, 1, 1),
    new Voxel(2, 2, 0, 1),
};
var rockMaterials = new[]
{
    VoxelMaterial.FromBase(Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.52, 0.48), 0.45),
    VoxelMaterial.FromBase(Color.FromRgb(0.34, 0.62, 0.28), 0.45),
};

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.05, 0.09));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "body":
        {
            // edge is 0 in the middle of the body and 1 at the silhouette - the
            // natural input for shading a round object.
            bottle.Fill(ctx, (x, y, edge) =>
            {
                if (bottle.InBand(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, fromY: 13, toY: 18, inset: 1.0))
                    return ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.42, 0.20), Colors.Black, edge * 0.5);
                var glass = y < 11 ? Color.FromRgb(0.90, 0.78, 0.50) : Color.FromRgb(0.92, 0.58, 0.18);
                return ColorOps.Lerp(glass, Color.FromRgb(0.36, 0.18, 0.06), edge * edge * 0.85);
            });
            // A highlight column, offset from the centre, sells the curvature.
            for (var y = (int)bottle.TopY; y <= bottle.BottomY; y++)
                ctx.PlotAA(12 - bottle.HalfWidthAt(y + 0.5) * 0.45, y + 0.5, Colors.White, 0.28);
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Glint((t % 3.0) / 3.0, 25, 2.0, strength: 0.35,
                mask: bottleMask));
            break;
        }

        case "blob":
        {
            // rim is large in the middle of a lobe and ~0 at the outline, so one
            // sample gives fill AND a darkened edge.
            canopy.Fill(ctx, (x, y, idx, dx, dy, rim) =>
            {
                var lit = MathH.Clamp01(0.55 - dx / 9.0 - dy / 8.0);
                var dapple = Scatter.Value(x, y, 2.0);
                var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.06, 0.22, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(0.42, 0.70, 0.30), lit);
                if (dapple > 0.7) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.60, 0.85, 0.40), 0.35);
                if (rim < 0.30) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Colors.Black, (0.30 - rim) / 0.30 * 0.6);
                return c;
            });
            ctx.DrawTaperedLine(12, 22, 12, 12, halfWidth: 1.6, taper: 0.45,
                colorLo: Color.FromRgb(0.46, 0.30, 0.16), colorHi: Color.FromRgb(0.18, 0.10, 0.05));
            break;
        }

        case "limb":
        {
            // Tapered limbs from one root, plus a supersampled sail on top to
            // show a procedural shape that no primitive covers.
            ctx.DrawTaperedLine(12, 23, 12, 13, 1.8, 0.5, Color.FromRgb(0.46, 0.30, 0.16), Color.FromRgb(0.18, 0.10, 0.05));
            for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++)
            {
                var a = -Math.PI / 2 + (i - 2) * 0.42 + Math.Sin(t * 0.6 + i) * 0.05;
                ctx.DrawTaperedLine(12, 14, 12 + Math.Cos(a) * 9, 14 + Math.Sin(a) * 9,
                    1.1, 0.8, Color.FromRgb(0.42, 0.28, 0.14), Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.09, 0.04));
            }
            var roll = Math.Sin(t * 0.9) * 0.25;
            var cos = Math.Cos(roll);
            var sin = Math.Sin(roll);
            ctx.FillSupersampled(4, 2, 20, 14, (px, py) =>
            {
                var dx = px - 12;
                var dy = py - 8;
                var lx = dx * cos + dy * sin;
                var ly = -dx * sin + dy * cos;
                if (Math.Abs(lx) > 0.6 && ly > -6 && ly < 6 && lx > 0.6 && lx < 5.5 - Math.Abs(ly) * 0.5)
                    return Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.95, 1.00);
                return Math.Abs(lx) <= 0.6 && ly > -6 && ly < 6 ? Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.70, 0.62) : (Color?)null;
            }, samples: 4, edgeBoost: 1.6);
            break;
        }

        case "voxel":
        {
            // Depth shifts a cube UP on the canvas, every cube paints a lit top
            // and a shaded front, and the model is painter-sorted.
            var breathe = 2.6 + Math.Sin(t) * 0.5;
            ctx.DrawVoxelSprite(rock, rockMaterials, x: 12, baseY: 20, scale: breathe,
                shade: c => Led.EnsureVisible(c, 0.08));
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Outline(Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.24, 0.30), 0.4));
            break;
        }
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.75);
};
```

### 21-motion-paths-and-physics

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo21MotionPathsPhysics
// displayName: Motion - Paths, Steering, Physics
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Follow a path, chase a target while avoiding obstacles, fall and bounce, and settle with a spring
// ---

// INTENT: Motion is what separates a picture from a scene. Four kinds, and they
// compose:
//
//   Path2D      walk a polyline by DISTANCE, not by index -> worms, rails,
//               orbits, a label following a curve. DrawTrail gives a body.
//   Steering    Seek / Arrive / Avoid / Wander return a velocity you add to
//               your own state -> things that look alive instead of scripted.
//   Geometry    the tests steering needs: InDisc, SegmentClearOfDisc,
//               PushOutOfDisc (the hard constraint that guarantees no overlap).
//   Ballistics  closed-form falling, throwing and bouncing - so the scene can
//               ask "when does it land" BEFORE it starts.
//   Spring      a value that chases a target with weight, overshoots slightly
//               and settles. The cure for motion that snaps.
//
// Everything with memory lives OUTSIDE the scene lambda.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("path", 4.0)
    .Add("steer", 5.0)
    .Add("fall", 4.0);

// A closed loop the worm walks along.
var loop = new Path2D(closed: true, (5, 6), (19, 5), (20, 17), (12, 21), (4, 16));

// Steering state: position and velocity of the chaser.
var px = 4.0;
var py = 4.0;
var vx = 0.0;
var vy = 0.0;

// Obstacles it must not enter.
var obstacles = new (double X, double Y, double R)[] { (12, 12, 3.5), (6, 17, 2.5), (18, 8, 2.5) };

// A spring that follows the chaser with weight - a camera dot.
var springX = new Spring(4.0, stiffness: 6.0, damping: 0.6);
var springY = new Spring(4.0, stiffness: 6.0, damping: 0.6);

// Integration steps use the MEASURED frame delta, capped - a nominal 1/Fps
// step drifts, and one slow frame must not teleport the simulation.
var clock = new FrameClock();

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.08));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "path":
        {
            // Draw the rail itself, then a body of segments trailing the head.
            for (var d = 0.0; d < loop.Length; d += 0.5)
            {
                var (rx, ry) = loop.At(d);
                ctx.PlotAA(rx, ry, Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.18, 0.28), 0.9);
            }
            var head = t * 9.0;
            loop.DrawTrail(ctx, head, segments: 8, spacing: 1.6,
                colorOf: i => ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.95, 0.70), Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.25, 0.35), i / 8.0),
                radius: 0.9);
            // A tangent-aligned marker: the head knows where it is going.
            var (hx, hy) = loop.At(head);
            var (tx, ty) = loop.TangentAt(head);
            ctx.PlotAA(hx + tx * 1.8, hy + ty * 1.8, Colors.White, 0.9);
            break;
        }

        case "steer":
        {
            // A target that moves slowly on its own.
            var targetX = 12 + Math.Cos(t * 0.5) * 8;
            var targetY = 12 + Math.Sin(t * 0.7) * 8;

            // Seek the target, push away from every obstacle, blend the two.
            var (sx, sy) = Steering.Arrive(px, py, targetX, targetY, maxSpeed: 9.0, slowRadius: 4.0);
            foreach (var o in obstacles)
            {
                var (ax, ay) = Steering.Avoid(px, py, o.X, o.Y, o.R + 3.0, strength: 16.0);
                sx += ax;
                sy += ay;
            }

            // Integrate with a little inertia so it does not turn on a dime.
            vx = MathH.Lerp(vx, sx, 0.25);
            vy = MathH.Lerp(vy, sy, 0.25);
            px = Math.Clamp(px + vx * dt, 0.5, 23.5);
            py = Math.Clamp(py + vy * dt, 0.5, 23.5);

            // HARD CONSTRAINT: whatever the steering did, never end up inside.
            foreach (var o in obstacles)
                (px, py) = Geometry.PushOutOfDisc(px, py, o.X, o.Y, o.R + 0.8);

            foreach (var o in obstacles)
                ctx.DrawCircle(o.X, o.Y, o.R, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.16, 0.24),
                    colorStroke: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.30, 0.45));

            // Green when the straight line to the target is clear, red when blocked.
            var clear = obstacles.All(o => Geometry.SegmentClearOfDisc(px, py, targetX, targetY, o.X, o.Y, o.R));
            ctx.DrawCircle(targetX, targetY, 1.2, colorFill: clear ? Colors.Lime : Colors.OrangeRed);

            // The spring dot lags behind - weight, without any extra state machine.
            ctx.PlotAA(springX.Step(px, dt), springY.Step(py, dt), Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.55, 1.00), 0.7);
            ctx.DrawCircle(px, py, 1.4, colorFill: Colors.White);
            break;
        }

        case "fall":
        {
            // A ball dropped from the top, losing energy on every bounce.
            var h = Ballistics.BounceHeight(cue.LocalSeconds, dropHeight: 16, gravity: 40, restitution: 0.62);
            ctx.DrawRectXyWh(0, 22, 24, 2, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.14, 0.12), isAntialias: false);
            ctx.DrawCircle(7, 21.5 - h, 1.8, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.20));

            // A thrown object: closed form, so its whole arc is known. The
            // parameters land it exactly at the 2 s loop point, on screen.
            var flight = cue.LocalSeconds % 2.0;
            var (thrownX, thrownY) = Ballistics.Throw(x0: 3, y0: 20, vx: 8.5, vy: -24.0, t: flight, gravity: 24);
            ctx.DrawCircle(thrownX, thrownY, 1.2, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.40, 0.90, 1.00));

            // Impact shake: the FLOOR jolts for a moment after every landing.
            var sinceHit = cue.LocalSeconds % 1.0;
            var (shx, shy) = Shake.At(sinceHit, amplitude: 1.4, duration: 0.28);
            ctx.DrawRectXyWh(shx, 22 + shy, 24, 2, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.34, 0.28, 0.22), isAntialias: false);
            break;
        }
    }

    ctx.DrawTextCentered(cue.Name, 18, Fonts.Var3x5, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.35));
};
```

### 22-automata-and-grids

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo22AutomataGrids
// displayName: Cellular Automata and Grids
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Life, falling sand and a dissolving logo - rules that produce new pictures forever
// ---

// INTENT: A cellular automaton is the cheapest source of endless, non-repeating
// content on a 24x24 panel: a handful of rules, no authored frames, and it never
// looks the same twice. CellGrid holds a byte per cell (0 = empty), so it works
// for alive/dead AND for materials, age or heat.
//
//   grid.Step((x, y, self, neighbours) => newValue)   simultaneous update
//   grid.StepLife()                                   Conway, as a one-liner
//   grid.StepSand()                                   grains fall and pile up
//   grid.SeedFrom(surface)                            start from a picture
//   grid.Draw(ctx, value => colour)                   render
//
// The double buffering matters: a cell must never see a half-updated
// neighbourhood, or the pattern turns into mush.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("life", 8.0)
    .Add("sand", 8.0);

// State outside the scene. Life wraps at the edges, sand must not.
var life = new CellGrid(24, 24);
var sand = new CellGrid(24, 24, wrap: false);
var lastCycle = -1L;

// Automata run on their OWN clock, not once per frame - 40 steps per second is
// far too fast to read. FixedStep quantises time into simulation steps.
var sim = new FixedStep(stepsPerSecond: 6.0);

// A logo the sand is seeded from, so the pile starts as a picture and collapses.
var logo = new BakedSurface(24, 24);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.06));

    // Reset both worlds at the start of every cycle.
    if (cue.Cycle != lastCycle)
    {
        lastCycle = cue.Cycle;
        life.Randomize(0.32, seed: (int)cue.Cycle * 17 + 3);
        logo.Ensure(cue.Cycle, s => s.DrawTextCentered("PXL", 7, Fonts.Mono6x6, Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.75, 0.30)));
        sand.Clear();
        sand.SeedFrom(logo.Surface, alphaThreshold: 0.4, value: 1);
    }

    // Six steps per second read well for life, fourteen for pouring sand.
    sim.StepsPerSecond = cue.Is("life") ? 6.0 : 14.0;
    var steps = sim.Due(ctx);

    if (cue.Is("life"))
    {
        for (var i = 0; i < steps; i++) life.StepLife();
        // Colour by neighbourhood density: dense clusters read warm, lone cells cool.
        life.Draw(ctx, (x, y, v) =>
        {
            if (v == 0) return null;
            var n = life.CountNeighbours(x, y);
            return ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.70, 1.00), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.20), n / 6.0);
        });
    }
    else
    {
        // Keep pouring new grains from the top so the pile keeps growing.
        for (var i = 0; i < steps; i++)
        {
            sand.StepSand();
            var col = 6 + (int)(Scatter.Value(sim.Count, 1.0) * 12);
            if (sand[col, 0] == 0) sand[col, 0] = 2;
        }
        sand.Draw(ctx, (x, y, v) => v switch
        {
            1 => Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.75, 0.30),
            2 => ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.85, 0.55, 0.25), Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.30, 0.12), Scatter.Value(x, y)),
            _ => null,
        });
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.6);
};
```

### 23-typography-and-clocks

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo23TypographyClocks
// displayName: Typography and Clocks
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Hand-set pixel digits, a rolling clock, a typewriter and a marquee
// ---

// INTENT: Text on 24x24 is a different craft from text on a screen. Four tools:
//
//   PixelFont     glyphs written as rows of '#' and '.', drawn pixel exact.
//                 When digits must hit exact pixels, a rasterised TTF is the
//                 wrong tool. PixelFont.Digits3x5 is built in.
//   RollingText   remembers when each character last changed, so a clock can
//                 ROLL over like an odometer instead of snapping.
//   TextMotion    Typewriter (with cursor), Marquee (scrolling with a gap),
//                 DigitRoll (the offset for one rolling character).
//   DrawTextContrast  paints text in the INVERSE brightness of the background,
//                 so a readout stays legible over a scene that changes all day.
//
// PixelFont.ToTargets also turns a word into particle targets - that is how a
// wordmark can assemble itself (see demo 19).

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("clock", 6.0)
    .Add("type", 4.0)
    .Add("loop", 5.0);

// Remembers per-character change times. Outside the scene, like all state.
var roll = new RollingText();

// A custom 3x5 alphabet for the marquee - only the letters this scene needs.
var letters = PixelFont.FromRows(3, 5, new Dictionary<char, string[]>
{
    ['P'] = ["###", "#.#", "###", "#..", "#.."],
    ['X'] = ["#.#", "#.#", ".#.", "#.#", "#.#"],
    ['L'] = ["#..", "#..", "#..", "#..", "###"],
    ['C'] = ["###", "#..", "#..", "#..", "###"],
    ['O'] = ["###", "#.#", "#.#", "#.#", "###"],
    ['K'] = ["#.#", "#.#", "##.", "#.#", "#.#"],
    [' '] = ["...", "...", "...", "...", "..."],
});

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    // A moving background, so the contrast readout has something to fight.
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(
            Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.05, 0.14), Color.FromRgb(0.38, 0.44, 0.62),
            MathH.Clamp01(Noise.Fbm(x * 0.09 + t * 0.15, y * 0.09, 3) * 1.4));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "clock":
        {
            // Seconds included so the roll is visible while you watch.
            var text = ctx.Now.ToString("HHmmss");
            roll.Update(text, t);

            // Draw each digit separately: a rolling one is drawn twice, the old
            // glyph sliding out upward and the new one coming in from below.
            for (var i = 0; i < text.Length; i++)
            {
                var (offset, from, to) = roll.At(i, t, duration: 0.28);
                var x = 1 + i * 4;
                var y = 9;
                if (offset <= 0)
                {
                    PixelFont.Digits3x5.Draw(ctx, to.ToString(), x, y, Colors.White);
                }
                else
                {
                    var shift = offset * 6.0;
                    PixelFont.Digits3x5.Draw(ctx, from.ToString(), x, (int)Math.Round(y - shift), Colors.White, 1.0 - offset);
                    PixelFont.Digits3x5.Draw(ctx, to.ToString(), x, (int)Math.Round(y + 6 - shift), Colors.White, offset);
                }
            }
            // The same time again as contrast text - readable on light AND dark.
            ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(ctx.Now.ToString("HH:mm"), 2, Fonts.Var4x5, alpha: 0.85);
            break;
        }

        case "type":
        {
            // Characters appear over time, with a blinking cursor while typing.
            var line1 = TextMotion.Typewriter("HELLO", cue.LocalSeconds, charsPerSecond: 5.0);
            var line2 = TextMotion.Typewriter("PIXEL", cue.LocalSeconds - 1.2, charsPerSecond: 5.0);
            // Var4x5 would make "HELLO" 25 px wide - one pixel too many.
            ctx.DrawTextCentered(line1, 6, Fonts.Var3x5, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 1.00, 0.60));
            ctx.DrawTextCentered(line2, 13, Fonts.Var3x5, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 1.00, 0.60));
            break;
        }

        case "loop":
        {
            // Draw the text twice, one gap apart, so the loop has no seam.
            const string message = "PXL CLOCK ";
            var width = letters.Measure(message);
            var (offset, total) = TextMotion.Marquee(width, ctx.Width, cue.LocalSeconds, pixelsPerSecond: 7.0, gap: 4);
            letters.Draw(ctx, message, (int)Math.Round(-offset), 10, Colors.White);
            letters.Draw(ctx, message, (int)Math.Round(-offset + total), 10, Colors.White);
            break;
        }
    }

    ctx.DrawTextCentered(cue.Name, 19, Fonts.Var3x5, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.4));
};
```

### 24-masks-light-and-sprites

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo24MasksLightSprites
// displayName: Masks, Rim Light, Sprites and Gauges
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Turn anything you drew into a mask, then light it, halo it, ground it - plus sprites written as text
// ---

// INTENT: A MASK answers "where is my subject" - and that is what lets you
// light, outline, halo and ground something WITHOUT knowing how it was drawn.
//
//   var before = ctx.Snapshot();
//   DrawSubject(ctx);
//   var subject = Mask.FromDiff(before, ctx);     // what did I just draw?
//   subject.DrawDropShadow(ctx, 1.5, 2.0);        // grounded
//   subject.DrawRimLight(ctx, warm, -60);         // three-dimensional
//   subject.DrawHalo(ctx, cool, radius: 2);       // separated from the background
//
// That trio - shadow, rim, halo - is the difference between a sticker and an
// object in a scene, and it costs three lines.
//
// PixelSprite writes a figure directly in the source as rows of characters with
// a colour table: no asset file, no loader, and it is readable in a diff.
//
// Gauges (bar, ring, dot row, perimeter) are how a value is shown on 24x24 -
// all of them read from two metres, a number does not.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

// A sprite is authored as text. '.' is transparent.
var cat = PixelSprite.FromRows(new[]
{
    ".g....g.",
    "gggggggg",
    "gwgggwgg",
    "gggggggg",
    ".gyyyyg.",
    "..g..g..",
}, new Dictionary<char, Color>
{
    ['g'] = Color.FromRgb(0.42, 0.38, 0.45),
    ['w'] = Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.95, 1.00),
    ['y'] = Color.FromRgb(0.85, 0.70, 0.35),
});

var perimeter = new PerimeterPath(24, 24, inset: 0);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    // 1) A busy background, so the mask work has something to fight.
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.09, 0.16), Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.30, 0.42),
            Noise.Fbm(x * 0.10 + t * 0.1, y * 0.10, 3));

    // A ridge line, drawn as a function - one call for a whole horizon.
    ctx.DrawFunctionLine(x => Shading.Ridge(x, 17.0, 3.5, 1.0, seed: 2.0),
        Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.18, 0.24), 0.9, thickness: 1.0);

    // 2) SNAPSHOT, draw the subject, DIFF - that is the mask.
    var before = ctx.Snapshot();

    // Walk fully off one edge and re-enter on the other - no visible teleport.
    var walkX = -8 + (int)((t * 3.0) % 33);
    var bob = (int)(Math.Sin(t * 6.0) * 0.5);
    cat.Draw(ctx, walkX, 12 + bob, flipX: false);

    var subject = Mask.FromDiff(before, ctx);

    // 3) The trio. Order matters: shadow first (behind), then rim, then halo.
    subject.DrawDropShadow(ctx, offsetX: 1.5, offsetY: 2.0, strength: 0.45);
    subject.DrawRimLight(ctx, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.90, 0.70), directionDegrees: -55, strength: 0.75);
    subject.DrawHalo(ctx, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.55, 0.95), radius: 2, strength: 0.30);

    // A contact shadow on the ground, right under the subject.
    for (var y = 17; y < 21; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var s = Shading.Contact(x + 0.5, y + 0.5, walkX + 4, 18.5, 4.0, 1.6);
        if (s > 0) ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(ctx[x, y], Colors.Black, s * 0.35);
    }

    // 4) Gauges. The perimeter is the clock: one dot per second around the frame.
    perimeter.DrawTicks(ctx, 12, Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.40, 0.50), 0.5);
    perimeter.DrawArc(ctx, ctx.Now.Second / 60.0, Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.85, 1.00), 0.85);
    var (hx, hy) = perimeter.AtValue(ctx.Now.Second, 60);
    ctx.DrawGlow(hx + 0.5, hy + 0.5, 2.0, Colors.White, layers: 3, coreAlpha: 0.9);

    // A scrim keeps the readout legible without hiding the scene.
    ctx.DrawScrim(1, 6, strength: 0.45);
    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(ctx.Now.ToString("HH:mm"), 2, Fonts.Var4x5, alpha: 0.9);

    ctx.DrawBarGauge(2, 21, 12, 2, (t % 5) / 5.0, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.85, 0.45), Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.24, 0.30));
    ctx.DrawDotRow(17, 22, 4, (int)(t % 5), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.70, 0.25), Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.18, 0.14));
};
```

### 25-recipe-weather-clock

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo25RecipeWeatherClock
// displayName: Recipe - Weather Clock
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A worked combination - time of day, weather, terrain, reflection, rare events and a perimeter clock
// ---

// INTENT: The individual demos each show ONE tool. This one shows the point of
// having them: a scene is a STACK of layers, and each layer is two or three
// lines because the mechanics come from the library.
//
// The stack, back to front - this order is the whole recipe:
//   1. DayCycle           one value that decides the mood of everything below
//   2. sky + stars        PhasePalette + StarField
//   3. terrain            Shading.Ridge, three layers with fog between them
//   4. wet ground         Filters.Mirror with a WaveField as distortion
//   5. weather            Weather.Rain / FogBank, in front of the world
//   6. rare event         Slots -> a lightning flash a few times a minute
//   7. readout            PerimeterPath seconds + DrawTextContrast time
//
// Change ONE thing - the day cycle, the weather intensity, the ridge seed - and
// the whole picture follows. That is what makes a scene feel authored rather
// than assembled.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const double horizonY = 15.0;
const double secondsPerDay = 30.0;   // 0 = run on the real wall clock

var skyTop = new PhasePalette(
    night: Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.09),
    twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.26, 0.15, 0.35),
    day: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.55, 0.90));

var skyLow = new PhasePalette(
    night: Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.06, 0.14),
    twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.50, 0.25),
    day: Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.90, 1.00));

var sun = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = horizonY, AmpX = 10, AmpY = 12 };
var stars = new StarField { Density = 0.05, TwinkleSpeed = 0.7 };
var puddle = new WaveField { OriginY = horizonY, Octaves = 2, Speed = 0.9, CrossStrength = 0.5, DomainWarp = 0.25 };
var rain = Weather.Rain(0.8);
var fog = new FogBank { CenterY = horizonY - 2.0, Thickness = 3.5, Density = 0.35, Speed = 0.9 };
var perimeter = new PerimeterPath(24, 24);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cycle = secondsPerDay > 0 ? DayCycle.Animated(ctx, secondsPerDay) : DayCycle.FromClock(ctx);
    var s = sun.At(cycle);
    var light = Lighting.FromAltitude(s.Altitude, startAltitude: -4.0, fullAltitude: 8.0);

    // 1) SKY
    var top = skyTop.Sample(cycle);
    var low = skyLow.Sample(cycle);
    for (var y = 0; y < (int)horizonY; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(top, low, MathH.Smoothstep(y / horizonY));

    stars.Draw(ctx, t, visibility: cycle.Night, maxY: (int)horizonY);

    if (s.Fade(5.0) > 0.01)
        ctx.DrawGlow(s.X, s.Y, 4.0, ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.5, 0.2), Colors.White, 1.0 - s.Lowness).WithAlpha(s.Fade(5.0)), layers: 3);

    // 2) TERRAIN: three ridge layers. Each one is darker and less hazy than the
    //    one behind it - that alone reads as distance.
    for (var layer = 0; layer < 3; layer++)
    {
        var amp = 4.5 - layer * 1.2;
        var baseY = horizonY - 3.0 + layer * 2.2;
        var haze = 0.55 - layer * 0.25;
        var body = light.Apply(ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.20, 0.26), Color.FromRgb(0.06, 0.08, 0.12), layer / 2.0), minAmbient: 0.18);
        var col = Fog.Apply(body, haze, low);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        {
            var crest = Shading.Ridge(x + 0.5, baseY, amp, 1.0 + layer * 0.5, seed: layer * 11.0);
            for (var y = (int)crest; y < (int)horizonY + 1; y++)
                if (ctx.IsInBounds(x, y)) ctx[x, y] = col;
            ctx.PlotAA(x + 0.5, crest, ColorOps.Lerp(col, Colors.White, 0.25 * light.Ambient), 0.6);
        }
    }

    // 3) WET GROUND: everything above the line, folded down and rippled.
    for (var y = (int)horizonY; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.06, 0.07, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.02, 0.04), (y - horizonY) / 9.0);

    ctx.Filter(Filters.Mirror(atY: horizonY, fade: 0.55, tint: low, tintStrength: 0.25,
        distortion: puddle, distortionStrength: 0.9, seconds: t));

    // 4) WEATHER in front of the world - lit by the SAME light as the terrain:
    //    bright drops at noon, faint streaks at night. Weather that ignores the
    //    scene light glows on top of the picture instead of sitting in it.
    fog.Color = light.Apply(Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.85, 0.92), minAmbient: 0.22);
    fog.Draw(ctx, t);
    rain.Color = light.Apply(Color.FromRgb(0.65, 0.80, 1.00), minAmbient: 0.25);
    // Perspective floor: far drops land at the horizon, near ones at the
    // bottom - the rain falls INTO the wet ground, not across it.
    rain.FloorFarY = horizonY + 0.5;
    rain.FloorNearY = 22.5;
    rain.Splash = 2.5;
    rain.Draw(ctx, t);

    // 5) RARE EVENT: a flash a few times a minute, deterministic, no state.
    var flash = Slots.Progress(t, slotSeconds: 7.0, chance: 0.55, duration: 0.35, seed: 3.0);
    if (flash >= 0)
    {
        var strength = (1.0 - flash) * (1.0 - flash);
        ctx.Filter(Filters.Fade(Color.FromRgb(0.85, 0.90, 1.00), strength * 0.5));
        // The bolt itself: a random walk down from the cloud line.
        var bx = 6 + Slots.Value(t, 7.0, 5.0) * 12;
        var by = 2.0;
        for (var i = 0; i < 10 && by < horizonY; i++)
        {
            var nx = bx + (Hash.From2D(Slots.Index(t, 7.0), i) - 0.5) * 3.0;
            var ny = by + 1.4;
            ctx.PlotAA(nx, ny, Colors.White, strength);
            bx = nx;
            by = ny;
        }
    }

    // 6) READOUT: seconds around the frame, time on a scrim.
    perimeter.DrawArc(ctx, ctx.Now.Second / 60.0, Color.FromRgb(0.45, 0.85, 1.00), 0.5);
    ctx.DrawScrim(17, 6, strength: 0.35);
    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(ctx.Now.ToString("HH:mm"), 18, Fonts.Var4x5, alpha: 0.9);
};
```

### 26-envelopes-and-microdrawing

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo26EnvelopesMicrodrawing
// displayName: Envelopes, Falloffs and Micro-drawing
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: The small curves and sub-pixel primitives that separate a polished scene from a rough one
// ---

// INTENT: Two families of small things that decide whether a scene looks
// finished:
//
// ENVELOPES - the shape of an event over its life. An easing goes from A to B;
// an envelope goes up, holds and comes back, which is what a flash, a spark, a
// pop or a gust actually does.
//   Envelope.Bell(p)          sin(p*pi) - the one-beat effect
//   Envelope.Spike(p, power)  a sharper bell
//   Envelope.RampHold(p, a, r)attack / hold / release
//   Envelope.Life(p, in, out) exactly 0 at both ends, so it loops cleanly
//   Envelope.Anticipate(p)    dips back, overshoots, settles
//   Envelope.Pulse(t, period) a repeating beat
//   Envelope.Twinkle(t, ...)  a sine to a high power: mostly dim, brief flares
//
// FALLOFFS - how something fades with distance: Gauss, Linear, Smooth, Ring
// (empty in the middle - shockwaves), Cone (a beam widening with depth).
//
// MICRO-DRAWING - below two pixels the normal primitives snap from cell to
// cell. PlotAA, PlotDiscAA, DrawSparkle, DrawGlowLine and DrawTextOutlined all
// work at sub-pixel accuracy, which is what lets small things MOVE smoothly.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("curve", 5.0)
    .Add("fade", 4.0)
    .Add("micro", 5.0);

var clock = new FrameClock();
var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);            // real frame delta, capped
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.07));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "curve":
        {
            // Five envelopes as bars, all driven by the same progress. Watching
            // them side by side is the fastest way to pick the right one.
            var p = (cue.LocalSeconds % 2.0) / 2.0;
            var values = new (string Name, double V, Color C)[]
            {
                ("bell", Envelope.Bell(p), Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.85, 1.00)),
                ("spike", Envelope.Spike(p, 4), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.75, 0.25)),
                ("hold", Envelope.RampHold(p, 0.2, 0.3), Color.FromRgb(0.55, 1.00, 0.55)),
                ("life", Envelope.Life(p, 0.15, 0.35), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.45, 0.55)),
                ("antic", Envelope.Anticipate(p), Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.60, 1.00)),
            };
            for (var i = 0; i < values.Length; i++)
            {
                // Anticipate dips below zero: anchor the bar at the baseline and
                // let it hang down, instead of detaching it.
                var h = values[i].V * 14.0;
                var top = h >= 0 ? 20 - h : 20;
                ctx.DrawRectXyWh(2 + i * 4, top, 3, Math.Abs(h) + 0.5, colorFill: values[i].C, isAntialias: false);
            }
            // A pulse and a twinkle as dots, so the difference is visible.
            ctx.PlotDiscAA(4, 3, 1.4, Colors.White, Envelope.Pulse(t, 1.2, 0.25));
            ctx.DrawSparkle(19, 3, Envelope.Twinkle(t, 2.0, 8.0), Colors.White, diagonal: true);
            break;
        }

        case "fade":
        {
            // A ring is a shockwave: empty in the middle, bright at the radius.
            var r = (cue.LocalSeconds % 2.0) / 2.0 * 14.0;
            for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var d = Math.Sqrt((x + 0.5 - 12) * (x + 0.5 - 12) + (y + 0.5 - 12) * (y + 0.5 - 12));
                var ring = Falloff.Ring(d, r, 2.0);
                var glow = Falloff.Gauss(d, 3.5) * 0.35;
                ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(ctx[x, y], Color.FromRgb(0.40, 0.85, 1.00), ring * 0.9 + glow);
            }
            // A cone: the shape of a beam on a surface.
            for (var y = 14; y < 24; y++)
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var k = Falloff.Cone(x + 0.5 - 12, y - 14, widthBase: 1.0, widthGrow: 0.8);
                if (k > 0.02) ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(ctx[x, y], Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.90, 0.60), k * 0.45);
            }
            break;
        }

        case "micro":
        {
            // Everything here moves sub-pixel: at 24x24 that is the difference
            // between "floating" and "stepping".
            var a = t * 1.2;
            ctx.DrawGlowLine(4, 22, 20, 22, Colors.White, Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.60, 1.00), 0.6, 3.0, 0.9);

            for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++)
            {
                // Arc interpolation: things travel on curves, not straight lines.
                var u = ((t * 0.4 + i * 0.2) % 1.0);
                var (px, py) = MotionShape.Arc(3, 16, 21, 16, u, bulge: -5 - i);
                ctx.PlotDiscAA(px, py, 1.1, ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.6, 0.2), Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.95, 0.7), u), Envelope.Life(u, 0.1, 0.2));
            }

            // Squash and stretch on a bouncing dot - volume stays constant.
            var bounce = Ballistics.BounceHeight(cue.LocalSeconds % 2.0, 10, 40, 0.6);
            var (sxs, sys) = MotionShape.SquashStretch(MathH.Clamp(bounce * 0.05 - 0.15, -0.3, 0.3));
            for (var oy = -2; oy <= 2; oy++)
            for (var ox = -2; ox <= 2; ox++)
            {
                var dx = ox / (2.0 * sxs);
                var dy = oy / (2.0 * sys);
                if (dx * dx + dy * dy > 1) continue;
                ctx.SetPixelSafe(6 + ox, (int)Math.Round(12 - bounce) + oy, Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.35, 0.45));
            }

            // Below the arcs and above the glow line - every element gets its
            // own band, nothing overlaps the segment label at the top.
            ctx.DrawTextOutlinedCentered("PXL", 17, Fonts.Var4x5, Color.FromRgb(0.35, 1.00, 0.75), Colors.Black, 0.95);
            break;
        }
    }

    ctx.DrawTextCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.35));
    // A rolling scanline over everything ties the three panels together.
    ctx.Filter(Filters.RollingScanline((t * 0.25) % 1.0, 5.0, 0.14));
};
```

### 27-voxel-models

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo27VoxelModels
// displayName: Voxel Models
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A voxel model written as text, rendered through an iso camera, lit by the scene's own sun
// ---

// INTENT: Real 3D voxel scenes from PLAIN TEXT. The pieces:
//
//   VoxModel.Parse("...")   the .vox text format: material lines (top/front/side
//                           colours), box fills, single voxels. Small enough to
//                           write by hand - or by a model - inside a pixogram.
//   IsoCamera               yaw / pitch / scale / pan, orthographic. The third
//                           member of the camera family (Camera2D, PinholeCamera).
//   VoxelLight              ambient + one directional light + hard shadows and
//                           ambient occlusion. VoxelLight.FromSkyBody(sun) derives
//                           it from the SAME SkyBody that drives the sky, so the
//                           whole scene agrees on where the light comes from.
//   model.Project(...)      voxel coordinates -> screen position, for overlays
//                           that follow the model while the camera moves.
//   model.ToTargets(...)    the rendered model as PixelTargets - so it can
//                           assemble from dust like any other picture.
//
// A rendered model re-sorts its faces every frame; for a STATIC shot, draw it
// once into a BakedSurface instead.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

// A lighthouse on a rock, written as text. Materials first, then geometry.
var model = VoxModel.Parse("""
    material rock   top=#8A8F98 front=#565B64 side=#41454D
    material rockdk top=#6E737C front=#45494F side=#34373D
    material white  top=#F2F4F6 front=#C9CDD3 side=#AFB3BB
    material red    top=#D84040 front=#A12929 side=#811F1F
    material lamp   top=#FFE070 front=#D9B94B side=#B99B39

    box 1 0 1  7 0 5  rock          # base slab
    box 2 1 2  6 1 4  rock          # second tier
    v 1 0 1 rockdk                  # dark accents on the rim
    v 7 0 5 rockdk
    v 2 1 4 rockdk
    box 3 2 2  4 3 3  white         # tower stripes, 2x2 footprint
    box 3 4 2  4 5 3  red
    box 3 6 2  4 7 3  white
    box 3 8 2  4 8 3  lamp          # lamp room
    box 3 9 2  4 9 3  red           # roof
    """);

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.3)
    .Add("orbit", 14.0)
    .Add("dust", 6.0);

var cam = new IsoCamera { Scale = 1.6, PanY = 1.0 };
var sun = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = 15, AmpX = 16, AmpY = 13 };
var skyTop = new PhasePalette(
    Color.FromRgb(0.01, 0.02, 0.07), Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.12, 0.32), Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.58, 0.95));
var skyLow = new PhasePalette(
    Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.05, 0.12), Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.35, 0.25), Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.88, 1.00));
var stars = new StarField { Density = 0.05, Brightness = 0.7 };

List<PixelTarget> targets = null;
PixelAssembly assembly = null;
var dustCycle = -1L;
var dustYaw = 0.0;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    // One DayCycle drives sky, sun, voxel light and the lamp - a full day per loop.
    var cycle = DayCycle.Animated(ctx, secondsPerDay: story.Total, startHour: 7.0);
    var s = sun.At(cycle);

    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var k = y / 23.0;
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(skyTop.Sample(cycle), skyLow.Sample(cycle), k);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) ctx[x, y] = col;
    }
    stars.Draw(ctx, t, visibility: cycle.Night, maxY: 14);

    if (cue.Is("orbit"))
    {
        // The camera orbits; the light is DERIVED from the sun's position, so
        // shading, sky and shadows always agree.
        cam.YawDegrees = 344.0 + t * 16.0;
        var light = VoxelLight.FromSkyBody(s, canvasWidth: ctx.WidthF);
        ctx.DrawVoxModel(model, cam, light);

        // The lamp: project the lamp room to the screen and glow at night.
        if (cycle.Night > 0.05)
        {
            var tip = model.Project(cam, 4.0, 8.5, 3.0, ctx.Width, ctx.Height);
            ctx.DrawGlow(tip.X, tip.Y, 2.5 + cycle.Night * 1.5, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.88, 0.45), coreAlpha: 0.8 * cycle.Night);
        }
        dustCycle = -1;
    }
    else
    {
        // Freeze the camera once per cycle, harvest the rendered model as
        // particle targets, and let it assemble from dust below.
        if (dustCycle != cue.Cycle)
        {
            dustCycle = cue.Cycle;
            dustYaw = cam.YawDegrees;
            // Harvest with the scene's CURRENT light, so the reassembled image
            // matches the time of day it froze at.
            targets = model.ToTargets(cam, ctx.Width, ctx.Height, VoxelLight.FromSkyBody(s, canvasWidth: ctx.WidthF));
            assembly = new PixelAssembly(targets)
            {
                Duration = 1.1,
                Spread = 9.0,
                FlightColor = Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.45),
                SourceOf = _ => (12.0, 26.0),
                DelayOf = i => Scatter.Value(targets[i].X, targets[i].Y) * 0.8,
            };
        }
        cam.YawDegrees = dustYaw;
        assembly.Draw(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.5);
};
```

### 28-vector-fields-and-verlet

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo28VectorFieldsVerlet
// displayName: Vector Fields and Verlet
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: One force field drives particles, a rope and a flag - wind you can see
// ---

// INTENT: Physics as SMALL COMPOSABLE PARTS instead of an engine.
//
//   IVectorField            direction + strength per position: the force
//                           connector. VectorField.Constant (wind), Swirl,
//                           Attract, Curl (divergence-free turbulence - THE
//                           smoke/ember field), Gradient(scalarField), Sum.
//   ParticleField.Force     particles ride the field.
//   Steering.Flow           an agent rides the same field.
//   VerletSystem            points + distance links: ropes, chains, flags,
//                           soft bodies. Pin points, add a Force, and use
//                           Constrain for HARD rules (never inside the rock).
//   Filters.Displace(field) the same wind smears a glow layer.
//
// The point of the connector: ONE wind blows on everything, so the scene reads
// as one weather instead of three separate effects. Verlet wants FIXED steps
// (FixedStep) - a variable frame delta makes cloth breathe.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.3)
    .Add("embers", 7.0)
    .Add("rope", 7.0)
    .Add("flag", 7.0);

// ONE wind for the whole scene: a steady breeze plus fast-drifting curl gusts.
var wind = VectorField.Sum(
    VectorField.Constant(8.0, -1.0),
    VectorField.Curl(scale: 0.18, strength: 9.0, driftSpeed: 1.1));

var embers = new ParticleField { Gravity = -6.0, Drag = 0.6, Force = wind };
var fireflyX = 6.0;
var fireflyY = 12.0;

var rope = VerletSystem.Rope(4, 2, 4, 19, segments: 12, pinStart: true);
rope.Force = wind;
rope.Constrain = p =>
{
    (p.X, p.Y) = Geometry.PushOutOfDisc(p.X, p.Y, 15, 14, 4.0);
    if (p.Y > 22.5) p.Y = 22.5;
};

var flag = VerletSystem.Grid(7, 4, cols: 7, rows: 5, spacing: 1.9, pin: (cx, _) => cx == 0);
flag.Force = wind;
flag.Gravity = 3.0;

var sim = new FixedStep(stepsPerSecond: 30);
var clock = new FrameClock();

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.08));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "embers":
        {
            // Ground fire feeds embers; the wind carries them up and around.
            // A WIDE source with jittered start speed - particles from the same
            // spot would all ride the same streamline and read as one string.
            if (ctx.CycleNo % 2 == 0)
                embers.Emit(
                    2 + Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 3.0) * 9.0,
                    21.5 + Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 5.0) * 2.0,
                    (Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 9.0) - 0.5) * 4.0,
                    -2 - Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 11.0) * 3.0,
                    life: 2.0 + Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 13.0) * 1.5,
                    Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55 + Scatter.Value(ctx.CycleNo, 7.0) * 0.3, 0.15), size: 1.0);
            embers.Step(ctx);
            embers.Draw(ctx, palette: Palettes.Fire, additive: true);

            // A firefly rides the SAME wind - one weather, two riders.
            var (vx, vy) = Steering.Flow(fireflyX, fireflyY, wind, t, maxSpeed: 6.0);
            fireflyX = MathH.Clamp(fireflyX + vx * dt, 1, 23);
            fireflyY = MathH.Clamp(fireflyY + vy * dt, 1, 23);
            if (fireflyX >= 22.9) fireflyX = 1.2;
            ctx.DrawSparkle(fireflyX, fireflyY, Envelope.Twinkle(t, 5.0, 4.0), Color.FromRgb(0.75, 1.00, 0.55));
            break;
        }

        case "rope":
        {
            // A rope in the wind, with a HARD rule: never inside the rock.
            foreach (var _ in sim.Steps(ctx)) rope.Step(1.0 / 30.0, t);

            ctx.DrawCircle(15, 14, 4.0, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.15, 0.20));
            ctx.DrawCircle(14, 13, 2.6, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.20, 0.26));
            foreach (var (a, b) in rope.Links)
                ctx.DrawGlowLine(a.X, a.Y, b.X, b.Y, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.45), Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.35, 0.10), 0.5, 1.6, 0.9);
            var anchor = rope.Points[0];
            ctx.PlotDiscAA(anchor.X, anchor.Y, 1.1, Colors.White, 0.9);
            break;
        }

        case "flag":
        {
            // A cloth grid pinned along the mast; the wind does the rest.
            foreach (var _ in sim.Steps(ctx)) flag.Step(1.0 / 30.0, t);

            ctx.DrawTaperedLine(6.5, 22, 6.5, 3, halfWidth: 0.7, taper: 0.25,
                colorLo: Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.52, 0.48), colorHi: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.28, 0.26));
            // Horizontal links row by row in stripe colours - the flag's fabric.
            var points = flag.Points;
            for (var cy = 0; cy < 5; cy++)
            {
                var stripe = cy % 2 == 0 ? Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.30, 0.25) : Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.92, 0.85);
                for (var cx = 0; cx < 6; cx++)
                {
                    var a = points[cy * 7 + cx];
                    var b = points[cy * 7 + cx + 1];
                    ctx.DrawLine(a.X, a.Y, b.X, b.Y, stripe);
                }
            }
            break;
        }
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.5);
};
```

### 29-palettes-and-panel-colour

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo29PalettesPanelColour
// displayName: Palettes and Panel Colour
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Palettes with stops, dithered sampling, HSL blending and the LED panel rules - side by side
// ---

// INTENT: Colour on a 24x24 LED panel is its own craft. Four lessons, each as
// a split comparison so the difference is VISIBLE:
//
//   Palette / stops        colour-over-value lookup; custom stops shift where
//                          the ramp turns. Palettes.* are ready-made ramps.
//   SampleDithered         ordered dithering INSTEAD of blending: a four-colour
//                          ramp stays four crisp colours and still reads smooth.
//   ColorOps.LerpHsl       blends around the colour wheel - Lerp through RGB
//                          passes through grey mud on opposite hues.
//   Led.EnsureVisible      very dark colours collapse to black on the panel;
//   Led.Quantize           keep silhouettes readable, posterize deliberately.
//
// Every band is labelled; the left half shows the naive way, the right half
// the panel-correct way.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("ramps", 7.0)
    .Add("blend", 7.0)
    .Add("panel", 7.0);

var fire = Palettes.Fire;
var custom = new Palette(
    [Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.05, 0.20), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.55, 0.75), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.95, 0.80)],
    [0.0, 0.75, 1.0]);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.03, 0.05));

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "ramps":
        {
            // Top: even stops. Middle: custom stops push the turn to the right.
            // Bottom: the same ramp dithered - four colours, no banding.
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var k = x / 23.0;
                for (var y = 3; y < 8; y++) ctx[x, y] = fire.Sample(k);
                for (var y = 9; y < 14; y++) ctx[x, y] = custom.Sample(k);
                for (var y = 15; y < 20; y++) ctx[x, y] = fire.SampleDithered(k, x, y);
            }
            ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered("RAMPS", 0, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.7);
            break;
        }

        case "blend":
        {
            // Blending orange toward cyan: RGB passes through grey, HSL stays
            // saturated all the way. The moving bar samples both.
            var a = Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.10);
            var b = Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.80, 0.95);
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var k = x / 23.0;
                for (var y = 4; y < 11; y++) ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.Lerp(a, b, k);
                for (var y = 13; y < 20; y++) ctx[x, y] = ColorOps.LerpHsl(a, b, k);
            }
            var probe = 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.Sin(t * 1.2);
            var px = probe * 23.0;
            ctx.DrawLine(px, 3, px, 20, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.35));
            ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered("RGB", 4, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.8);
            ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered("HSL", 14, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.8);
            break;
        }

        case "panel":
        {
            // A night silhouette drawn twice: naive (collapses to black) and
            // with EnsureVisible. Below: deliberate posterize via Quantize.
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var crest = Shading.Ridge(x, 8.0, amplitude: 2.5, roughness: 1.2, seed: 6.0);
                var naive = Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.06);
                for (var y = (int)crest; y < 11; y++)
                {
                    var c = x < 12 ? naive : Led.EnsureVisible(naive, 0.10);
                    ctx.SetPixelSafe(x, y, c);
                }
            }
            ctx.DrawLine(12, 2, 12, 10, Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.25));
            for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
            {
                var k = x / 23.0;
                var smooth = Palettes.Sunset.Sample(k);
                for (var y = 13; y < 16; y++) ctx[x, y] = smooth;
                for (var y = 17; y < 20; y++) ctx[x, y] = Led.Quantize(smooth, levels: 5);
            }
            ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered("PANEL", 21, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.7);
            break;
        }
    }
};
```

### 30-timing-and-rare-events

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo30TimingRareEvents
// displayName: Timing and Rare Events
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: The four timing tools in one scene - fixed steps, measured deltas, change triggers and jittered rare events
// ---

// INTENT: Four DIFFERENT timing problems, four dedicated tools - using the
// wrong one is where scenes stutter or drift:
//
//   FixedStep       a simulation at its OWN rate (the pulsing grid below runs
//                   at 8 steps per second, readable, frame rate independent).
//   FrameClock      the MEASURED frame delta, capped - integrate motion with
//                   it and one slow frame cannot teleport anything.
//   ChangeTrigger   fires exactly ONCE when a value changes - the second tick
//                   spawns one spark ring, not forty.
//   Slots           rare events on a stable, jittered schedule - the shooting
//                   star a few times a minute, derived from time, no state.
//
// Everything here is deterministic except the physics dot - watch how each
// panel moves at its own honest pace.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var sim = new FixedStep(stepsPerSecond: 8);
var clock = new FrameClock();
var tick = new ChangeTrigger<int>();
var sparks = new ParticleField { Gravity = 0.0, Drag = 2.2 };

var gridPhase = 0;
var dotX = 3.0;
var dotV = 5.0;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.07));

    // 1) FixedStep: a checker grid that advances 8 times a second - its pace
    //    stays identical whether the scene renders at 10 or 60 fps.
    foreach (var _ in sim.Steps(ctx)) gridPhase++;
    for (var y = 0; y < 5; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 5; x++)
    {
        var on = (x + y + gridPhase) % 2 == 0;
        ctx.DrawRectXyWh(1 + x * 2, 1 + y * 2, 2, 2,
            colorFill: on ? Color.FromRgb(0.20, 0.55, 0.85) : Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.09, 0.16), isAntialias: false);
    }

    // 2) FrameClock: a dot integrated with the MEASURED delta bounces between
    //    two walls - never faster, never slower, never through the wall.
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);
    dotX += dotV * dt;
    if (dotX > 21.5) { dotX = 21.5; dotV = -dotV; }
    if (dotX < 14.5) { dotX = 14.5; dotV = -dotV; }
    ctx.DrawRectXyWh(14, 2, 8, 5, colorStroke: Color.FromRgb(0.25, 0.30, 0.40), strokeWidth: 1, isAntialias: false);
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(dotX, 4.5, 1.2, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.75, 0.25));

    // 3) ChangeTrigger: exactly one spark ring per second tick.
    if (tick.Changed(ctx.Now.Second))
        sparks.Burst(12, 14, count: 14, speed: 8.0, Color.FromRgb(0.55, 1.00, 0.70), life: 0.5, spreadDegrees: 360);
    sparks.Step(ctx);
    sparks.Draw(ctx, additive: true);
    ctx.DrawTextCentered(ctx.Now.Second.ToString("00"), 12, Fonts.Mono4x5, Color.FromRgb(0.55, 1.00, 0.70));

    // 4) Slots: a shooting star roughly every seven seconds, jittered - the
    //    progress value drives position AND fade, nothing is remembered.
    var p = Slots.Progress(t, slotSeconds: 7.0, chance: 0.7, duration: 0.9, seed: 5.0);
    if (p >= 0)
    {
        var sx = MathH.Lerp(2.0, 22.0, p);
```
