```csharp
        var sy = MathH.Lerp(19.0, 22.5, p);
        ctx.DrawGlowLine(sx - 2.5, sy - 0.8, sx, sy, Colors.White, Color.FromRgb(0.45, 0.65, 1.00),
            coreWidth: 0.5, glowWidth: 1.6, alpha: Envelope.Bell(p));
    }
};
```

### 31-camera-direction

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo31CameraDirection
// displayName: Camera Direction
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: The camera as a storyteller - follow, hold, zoom onto an event, shake on impact, cut back wide
// ---

// INTENT: A scene painted ONCE at world size, and everything after that is
// CAMERA LANGUAGE on top of it:
//
//   Camera2D.Focus       a shot is just centre + zoom.
//   cam.LerpTo           the cut between shots is an eased travel, not a jump.
//   WorldToScreen        overlays (a marker, a label) follow a world position
//                        through every camera move.
//   Shake.At             an impact kicks the camera, not the world.
//
// The storyboard cycles: wide establishing shot -> follow the runner ->
// zoom onto the beacon as it flares -> back to wide. One world, four shots.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.3)
    .Add("wide", 4.0)
    .Add("follow", 6.0)
    .Add("beacon", 5.0)
    .Add("return", 3.0);

var world = new BakedSurface(72, 40);
var wide = Camera2D.Focus(36, 20, zoom: 0.6);   // 24 / zoom = 40 world pixels: full height, no letterbox
var cam = Camera2D.Focus(36, 20, zoom: 0.6);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    world.Ensure("landscape", s =>
    {
        for (var y = 0; y < 40; y++)
        {
            var col = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.05, 0.13), Color.FromRgb(0.13, 0.10, 0.24), y / 39.0);
            for (var x = 0; x < 72; x++) s[x, y] = col;
        }
        for (var x = 0; x < 72; x++)
        {
            var crest = Shading.Ridge(x, 26.0, amplitude: 4.0, roughness: 0.8, seed: 9.0);
            for (var y = (int)crest; y < 40; y++)
                s.SetPixelSafe(x, y, Color.FromRgb(0.11, 0.14, 0.21));
            s.PlotAA(x + 0.5, crest, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.36, 0.48), 0.7);
        }
        for (var i = 0; i < 40; i++)
        {
            var sx = Hash.From2D(i, 1.0) * 72.0;
            var sy = Hash.From2D(i, 2.0) * 20.0;
            s.PlotAA(sx, sy, Colors.White, 0.25 + Hash.From2D(i, 3.0) * 0.4);
        }
        s.DrawGlow(58, 22, 2.5, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.20), coreAlpha: 0.8);
        s.DrawTaperedLine(58, 26, 58, 22, halfWidth: 0.6, taper: 0.3,
            colorLo: Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.30, 0.28), colorHi: Color.FromRgb(0.18, 0.15, 0.14));
    });

    // The runner travels the ridge; the beacon flares during its shot.
    var runnerX = 8.0 + (t * 4.0) % 60.0;
    var runnerY = Shading.Ridge(runnerX, 26.0, 4.0, 0.8, 9.0) - 1.0;
    var flare = cue.Is("beacon") ? Envelope.Bell(cue.Progress) : 0.0;

    // CAMERA LANGUAGE: pick the target shot, then travel toward it.
    var target = cue.Name switch
    {
        "follow" => Camera2D.Focus(runnerX, runnerY - 1.5, zoom: 1.0),
        "beacon" => Camera2D.Focus(58, 22, zoom: 1.35),
        _ => wide,
    };
    cam = cam.LerpTo(target, 0.12);   // ease a little closer every frame - the cut becomes a travel

    // The impact of the flare kicks the camera, not the world.
    if (flare > 0.0)
    {
        var (sx, sy) = Shake.At(cue.LocalSeconds, amplitude: flare * 1.2, duration: cue.Duration);
        cam.CenterX += sx;
        cam.CenterY += sy;
    }

    ctx.DrawSurface(world.Surface, cam);

    // World-locked overlays: they follow through every move.
    var (rx, ry) = cam.WorldToScreen(runnerX, runnerY, ctx.WidthF, ctx.HeightF);
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(rx, ry, 1.0, Color.FromRgb(0.55, 1.00, 0.70));
    if (flare > 0.0)
    {
        var (bx, by) = cam.WorldToScreen(58, 22, ctx.WidthF, ctx.HeightF);
        ctx.DrawGlow(bx, by, 3.0 + flare * 3.0, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.60, 0.20), coreAlpha: 0.5 + flare * 0.5);
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.55);
};
```

### 32-sprites-and-characters

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo32SpritesCharacters
// displayName: Sprites and Characters
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A character authored as text rows, animated frame by frame, lit like an object, dissolved to dust
// ---

// INTENT: The picture IS the code. A PixelSprite is glyph rows plus a colour
// table - reviewable in a diff, no asset file:
//
//   PixelSprite.FromRows   author a character in-source.
//   SpriteAnimation        a walk cycle is just frames at an fps.
//   Draw / flipX / tint    the same sprite walks both ways, flashes on hits.
//   ToMask                 the sprite becomes a Mask: drop shadow, rim light
//                          and halo make it an OBJECT in the scene.
//   ToTargets              the sprite becomes PixelTargets: it dissolves and
//                          reassembles like any other picture.
//
// One little robot, walking, lit, dissolving - all from ten rows of text.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var palette = new Dictionary<char, Color>
{
    ['b'] = Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.75, 0.95),
    ['d'] = Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.38, 0.55),
    ['e'] = Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.30),
    ['g'] = Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.60, 0.68),
};

var standing = PixelSprite.FromRows([
    ".bbbb.",
    "beebeb",
    "bbbbbb",
    ".dddd.",
    "dbbbbd",
    "dbbbbd",
    ".d..d.",
    ".g..g.",
], palette);

var stepping = PixelSprite.FromRows([
    ".bbbb.",
    "beebeb",
    "bbbbbb",
    ".dddd.",
    "dbbbbd",
    "dbbbbd",
    ".d.d..",
    ".g..g.",
], palette);

var walk = new SpriteAnimation(6.0, standing, stepping);

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.3)
    .Add("walk", 8.0)
    .Add("dust", 6.0);

List<PixelTarget> targets = null;
PixelAssembly assembly = null;
var dustCycle = -1L;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.04, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.02, 0.05), y / 23.0);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) ctx[x, y] = col;
    }
    ctx.DrawRectXyWh(0, 19, 24, 5, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.09, 0.08, 0.13), isAntialias: false);

    if (cue.Is("walk"))
    {
        // Walk fully off one edge and re-enter on the other; flip on direction.
        var span = 40.0;
        var k = (t * 5.0) % (span * 2.0);
        var forward = k < span;
        var x = forward ? -8.0 + k : 32.0 - (k - span);
        var frame = walk.At(t);
        var sy = 11 + (int)(Math.Sin(t * 9.0) * 0.5 + 0.5);

        // The mask trio makes the sprite an object: shadow below, rim above.
        var mask = frame.ToMask(ctx.Width, ctx.Height, (int)x, sy, flipX: !forward);
        mask.DrawDropShadow(ctx, offsetX: 1.0, offsetY: 1.5, strength: 0.5);
        frame.Draw(ctx, (int)x, sy, flipX: !forward);
        mask.DrawRimLight(ctx, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.90, 0.70), directionDegrees: -60, strength: 0.7);
        dustCycle = -1;
    }
    else
    {
        // Freeze once per cycle, harvest, reassemble from dust.
        if (dustCycle != cue.Cycle)
        {
            dustCycle = cue.Cycle;
            targets = standing.ToTargets(9, 11);
            assembly = new PixelAssembly(targets)
            {
                Duration = 1.0,
                Spread = 8.0,
                FlightColor = Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.85, 1.00),
                SourceOf = _ => (12.0, 26.0),
                DelayOf = i => Scatter.Value(targets[i].X, targets[i].Y) * 0.7,
            };
        }
        assembly.Draw(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.55);
};
```

### 33-gauges-and-readouts

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo33GaugesReadouts
// displayName: Gauges and Readouts
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Every readout that carries from two metres - bar, ring, dot row, perimeter ring and a scrimmed number
// ---

// INTENT: A number is the LEAST readable thing on a 24x24 panel from two
// metres. These read instantly:
//
//   DrawBarGauge     a filled bar with a frame - level, progress, volume.
//   DrawRingGauge    a circular arc - the classic dial.
//   DrawDotRow       N of M dots lit - weekday, lives, steps.
//   PerimeterPath    the canvas BORDER as a dial: DrawArc for progress,
//                    DrawTicks for the scale, AtFraction for the head marker.
//   DrawScrim        the number that IS needed sits on a scrim, measured
//                    and centred - never on a hand-picked x.
//
// All gauges show the same live value, so the eye can compare how each one
// reads. The value breathes on an Envelope so every state appears.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var ring = new PerimeterPath(24, 24);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.08));

    // One live value in [0, 1] drives every gauge - rises, holds, falls.
    var value = Envelope.RampHold((t % 9.0) / 9.0, attack: 0.35, release: 0.35);
    var accent = Palettes.Heat.Sample(value);

    // The canvas border as the outermost dial.
    ring.DrawTicks(ctx, count: 12, Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.18, 0.24));
    ring.DrawArc(ctx, value, accent, alpha: 0.9);
    var (hx, hy) = ring.AtFraction(value);
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(hx, hy, 1.0, Colors.White, 0.9);

    // Bar: left. Ring dial: right. Both from the same value.
    ctx.DrawBarGauge(3, 4, width: 3, height: 12, value: value, fill: accent,
        frame: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.34, 0.42), background: Color.FromRgb(0.07, 0.08, 0.12));
    ctx.DrawRingGauge(15, 9, radius: 4.5, value: value, fill: accent,
        track: Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.12, 0.18), thickness: 1.4);

    // Dot row: the value in five coarse steps.
    ctx.DrawDotRow(7, 18, count: 5, lit: (int)Math.Round(value * 5.0),
        accent, Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.13, 0.18), spacing: 2.5);

    // And the number itself - measured, centred, on a scrim.
    ctx.DrawScrim(20, 4, strength: 0.55);
    ctx.DrawTextCentered($"{(int)(value * 100),3}", 20, Fonts.Var3x5, Colors.White);
};
```

### 34-variants-as-data

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo34VariantsAsData
// displayName: Variants as Data
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Three moods of one landscape as data rows - a new variant is one more entry, not another branch
// ---

// INTENT: Scene variants belong in a DATA TABLE, not in a switch. Each row
// below is (name, sky, ground, accent, star density) - the drawing code exists
// ONCE and reads the row:
//
//   variants[]        the content. Adding "desert dawn" is one more line.
//   CyclePicker       picks a different variant every cycle, avoiding repeats.
//   Stagger.Spread    the landscape elements pop in one after another on
//                     every variant change - the reveal choreography is also
//                     written once.
//
// This is the pattern that keeps big scenes maintainable: mechanics once,
// content as rows.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var variants = new (string Name, Color SkyTop, Color SkyLow, Color Ground, Color Accent, double Stars)[]
{
    ("night", Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(0.07, 0.08, 0.18), Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.14, 0.24), Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.75, 1.00), 0.05),
    ("ember", Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.03, 0.05), Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.16, 0.08), Color.FromRgb(0.22, 0.10, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.55, 0.20), 0.01),
    ("mint",  Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.08, 0.07), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.30, 0.24), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.22, 0.17), Color.FromRgb(0.45, 1.00, 0.75), 0.02),
};

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.4).Add("scene", 7.0);
var picker = new CyclePicker(variants.Length);
var stars = new StarField { Brightness = 0.7 };

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);
    picker.Update(cue.Cycle);
    var v = variants[picker.Current];

    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(v.SkyTop, v.SkyLow, MathH.Smoothstep(y / 23.0));
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) ctx[x, y] = col;
    }
    stars.Density = v.Stars;
    stars.Draw(ctx, t, maxY: 14);

    // Three ridge layers and three trees pop in staggered on every change.
    for (var layer = 0; layer < 3; layer++)
    {
        var reveal = Stagger.Spread(layer, 6, cue.LocalSeconds, totalSeconds: 1.5, overlap: 0.5);
        if (reveal <= 0) continue;
        var baseY = 13.0 + layer * 3.5;
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(v.Ground, Colors.Black, layer * 0.25);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        {
            var crest = Shading.Ridge(x, baseY, amplitude: 2.0 + layer, roughness: 1.0, seed: layer * 7.0);
            var lift = (1.0 - Easings.EaseOutBack(reveal)) * 6.0;
            for (var y = (int)(crest + lift); y < 24; y++)
                ctx.SetPixelSafe(x, y, col);
            ctx.PlotAA(x + 0.5, crest + lift, ColorOps.Lerp(col, v.Accent, 0.30), 0.6);
        }
    }
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++)
    {
        var reveal = Stagger.Spread(3 + i, 6, cue.LocalSeconds, totalSeconds: 1.5, overlap: 0.5);
        if (reveal <= 0) continue;
        var k = Easings.EaseOutBack(reveal);
        var tx = 4.0 + i * 8.0;
        var ty = Shading.Ridge(tx, 13.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.0);
        ctx.DrawTaperedLine(tx, ty, tx, ty - 4.0 * k, halfWidth: 0.6, taper: 0.6,
            colorLo: v.Accent, colorHi: ColorOps.Lerp(v.Accent, Colors.Black, 0.4));
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(v.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.6);
};
```

### 35-steering-and-swarms

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo35SteeringSwarms
// displayName: Steering and Swarms
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: A school of fish from three steering rules - seek the leader, avoid the rocks, never overlap
// ---

// INTENT: Life-like group movement is a SUM OF VELOCITIES, not a script:
//
//   Steering.Seek      every fish steers toward the leader...
//   Steering.Wander    ...the leader itself drifts on smooth noise.
//   Steering.Avoid     rocks push back, weighted by distance.
//   Steering.Flow      a gentle current (an IVectorField) moves the whole
//                      school sideways - one more velocity in the sum.
//   Geometry.PushOutOfDisc   the HARD rule applied after integration:
//                      whatever the sum said, nobody ends up inside a rock.
//
// Velocities add, constraints clamp - that order is the whole secret.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var rocks = new (double X, double Y, double R)[] { (7, 15, 3.0), (17, 8, 2.6) };
var current = VectorField.Curl(scale: 0.12, strength: 2.5, driftSpeed: 0.4);

var fish = new (double X, double Y)[9];
for (var i = 0; i < fish.Length; i++)
    fish[i] = (4 + (i % 3) * 2.5, 6 + i / 3 * 2.5);

var clock = new FrameClock();

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);

    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.07, 0.12), Color.FromRgb(0.01, 0.03, 0.06), y / 23.0);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) ctx[x, y] = col;
    }
    foreach (var (rx, ry, rr) in rocks)
    {
        ctx.DrawCircle(rx, ry, rr, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.12, 0.15));
        ctx.DrawCircle(rx - rr * 0.3, ry - rr * 0.3, rr * 0.5, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.14, 0.17, 0.21));
    }

    // The leader wanders smoothly; the school seeks it.
    var (wx, wy) = Steering.Wander(t, seed: 2.0, speed: 0.11);
    var leaderX = 12.0 + wx * 8.5;
    var leaderY = 12.0 + wy * 7.5;

    for (var i = 0; i < fish.Length; i++)
    {
        var (fx, fy) = fish[i];

        // 1) The sum of velocities: goal + current + all the rock repulsions.
        var (sx, sy) = Steering.Seek(fx, fy, leaderX, leaderY, maxSpeed: 7.0);
        var (cx, cy) = Steering.Flow(fx, fy, current, t, maxSpeed: 2.5);
        var vx = sx + cx;
        var vy = sy + cy;
        foreach (var (rx, ry, rr) in rocks)
        {
            var (ax, ay) = Steering.Avoid(fx, fy, rx, ry, rr + 3.0, strength: 14.0);
            vx += ax;
            vy += ay;
        }

        // 2) Integrate, then the HARD constraint - never inside a rock.
        fx += vx * dt;
        fy += vy * dt;
        foreach (var (rx, ry, rr) in rocks)
            (fx, fy) = Geometry.PushOutOfDisc(fx, fy, rx, ry, rr + 0.6);
        fx = MathH.Clamp(fx, 0.5, 23.5);
        fy = MathH.Clamp(fy, 0.5, 23.5);
        fish[i] = (fx, fy);

        // A fish is a bright head with a dim tail against the swim direction.
        var len = Math.Sqrt(vx * vx + vy * vy);
        var (tx, ty) = len > 0.1 ? (fx - vx / len * 1.3, fy - vy / len * 1.3) : (fx - 1.0, fy);
        var tone = 0.75 + Scatter.Value(i, 5.0) * 0.25;
        ctx.PlotAA(tx, ty, Color.FromRgb(0.20 * tone, 0.45 * tone, 0.60 * tone), 0.7);
        ctx.PlotDiscAA(fx, fy, 0.8, Color.FromRgb(0.45 * tone, 0.85 * tone, 1.00 * tone));
    }

    ctx.PlotDiscAA(leaderX, leaderY, 0.9, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.80, 0.35), 0.9);
};
```

### 36-deterministic-textures

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo36DeterministicTextures
// displayName: Deterministic Textures
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Stone, grass, rust and water surface from Hash, Noise and Scatter - rich texture, zero flicker
// ---

// INTENT: Texture on a small panel must be DETERMINISTIC - the same pixel the
// same every frame, or the whole surface boils. Three tools, layered:
//
//   Hash.From2D     one stable random number per cell - the atom.
//   Noise.Fbm       smooth fractal fields - the body of every material.
//   Noise.Ridged    sharp crests - cracks, veins, mountain lines.
//   Scatter         "is this pixel one of the few" - flecks, blades, glints,
//                   with Scatter.Pick choosing WHICH kind deterministically.
//
// Four material swatches, each built from the same three tools with different
// numbers - and because z is time, the water drifts WITHOUT flickering.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    ctx.DrawBackground(Colors.Black);

    // STONE (top left): low-frequency body + ridged cracks + rare pale flecks.
    for (var y = 0; y < 12; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 12; x++)
    {
        var body = Noise.Fbm(x * 0.28, y * 0.28, 3);
        var crack = Noise.Ridged(x * 0.35 + 40.0, y * 0.35, 3);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.24, 0.24, 0.27), Color.FromRgb(0.40, 0.39, 0.42), body);
        if (crack > 0.62) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Colors.Black, 0.5);
        if (Scatter.Has(x, y, 0.05, seed: 1.0)) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.55, 0.54, 0.58), 0.6);
        ctx[x, y] = c;
    }

    // GRASS (top right): vertical streaks from per-column hash + scattered blades.
    for (var y = 0; y < 12; y++)
    for (var x = 12; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var column = Hash.From2D(x, 7.0);
        var body = Noise.Fbm(x * 0.30, y * 0.55, 2);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.07, 0.22, 0.09), Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.42, 0.14), body * 0.7 + column * 0.3);
        if (Scatter.Has(x, y, 0.08, seed: 2.0))
            c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.45, 0.75, 0.25), 0.5 + 0.5 * Envelope.Twinkle(t, 1.5, phase: x * 3.1));
        ctx[x, y] = c;
    }

    // RUST (bottom left): metal and oxide fight over the surface - and
    // Scatter.Pick decides which fleck type a pixel carries.
    for (var y = 12; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 12; x++)
    {
        var oxide = Noise.Fbm(x * 0.22 + 90.0, y * 0.22, 4);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.32, 0.33, 0.36), Color.FromRgb(0.45, 0.20, 0.08), MathH.Smoothstep(oxide));
        var fleck = Scatter.Pick(x, y, 0.90, 0.06, 0.04);
        if (fleck == 1) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.70, 0.35, 0.12), 0.7);
        if (fleck == 2) c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.60, 0.62, 0.66), 0.6);
        ctx[x, y] = c;
    }

    // WATER (bottom right): the SAME tools, but z = time - the field drifts,
    // crests glint, and nothing ever flickers because x/y stay integral.
    for (var y = 12; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 12; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var wave = Noise.Fbm(x * 0.20, y * 0.20, t * 0.35, 3);
        var c = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.12, 0.22), Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.35, 0.50), wave);
        if (wave > 0.62 && Scatter.Has(x, y, 0.30, seed: 4.0))
            c = ColorOps.Lerp(c, Color.FromRgb(0.75, 0.95, 1.00), 0.55);
        ctx[x, y] = c;
    }

    // Swatch frame.
    ctx.DrawLine(12, 0, 12, 24, Colors.Black.WithAlpha(0.6));
    ctx.DrawLine(0, 12, 24, 12, Colors.Black.WithAlpha(0.6));
};
```

### 37-parallax-layers

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo37ParallaxLayers
// displayName: Parallax Layers
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Three baked world strips, one camera value, three speeds - depth from parallax alone
// ---

// INTENT: Stage & camera, lesson two: PARALLAX. Depth needs no 3D - it needs
// layers that move at different speeds:
//
//   Three transparent surfaces (sky ridge, forest, fence), each baked ONCE
//   at world width. One travel value drives three Camera2D positions - the
//   far layer crawls, the near layer rushes. That speed ratio IS the depth.
//
//   Transparent surfaces stack: pixels with alpha 0 let the layer behind
//   show through, so the composite is just three DrawSurface calls.
//
// Compare with 17 (PinholeCamera): that projects real 3D positions; parallax
// fakes the same feeling from flat strips at a fraction of the effort.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const int worldW = 96;

var far = new BakedSurface(worldW, 24);
var mid = new BakedSurface(worldW, 24);
var near = new BakedSurface(worldW, 24);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    far.Ensure("ridge", s =>
    {
        s.Clear(Colors.Transparent);
        for (var x = 0; x < worldW; x++)
        {
            var crest = Shading.Ridge(x, 13.0, amplitude: 3.0, roughness: 0.7, seed: 3.0);
            for (var y = (int)crest; y < 24; y++)
                s.SetPixelSafe(x, y, Color.FromRgb(0.13, 0.15, 0.26));
        }
    });
    mid.Ensure("forest", s =>
    {
        s.Clear(Colors.Transparent);
        for (var x = 0; x < worldW; x++)
        {
            var crest = Shading.Ridge(x, 17.0, amplitude: 2.0, roughness: 1.6, seed: 8.0);
            for (var y = (int)crest; y < 24; y++)
                s.SetPixelSafe(x, y, Color.FromRgb(0.07, 0.11, 0.13));
        }
        for (var i = 0; i < 26; i++)
        {
            var tx = Hash.From2D(i, 5.0) * worldW;
            var ty = Shading.Ridge(tx, 17.0, 2.0, 1.6, 8.0);
            s.DrawTaperedLine(tx, ty + 1, tx, ty - 2.5, halfWidth: 0.7, taper: 0.7,
                colorLo: Color.FromRgb(0.10, 0.16, 0.14), colorHi: Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.09, 0.08));
        }
    });
    near.Ensure("fence", s =>
    {
        s.Clear(Colors.Transparent);
        for (var x = 0; x < worldW; x += 6)
            s.DrawRectXyWh(x, 19, 1, 5, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.05), isAntialias: false);
        s.DrawRectXyWh(0, 21, worldW, 1, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.05, 0.06), isAntialias: false);
    });

    // Sky behind everything.
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.05, 0.04, 0.14), Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.13, 0.22), y / 23.0);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) ctx[x, y] = col;
    }
    ctx.DrawGlow(6, 5, 2.2, Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.90, 0.80), coreAlpha: 0.8);

    // ONE travel value in [0, 1], eased back and forth - and three DEPTH
    // FACTORS. The near layer sweeps the full strip, the far one barely moves;
    // that ratio is the whole parallax effect.
    var travel = (1.0 - Math.Cos(t * 0.30)) * 0.5;
    double CamX(double depth) => 12.0 + travel * (worldW - 24.0) * depth;
    ctx.DrawSurface(far.Surface, Camera2D.Focus(CamX(0.25), 12));
    ctx.DrawSurface(mid.Surface, Camera2D.Focus(CamX(0.55), 12));
    ctx.DrawSurface(near.Surface, Camera2D.Focus(CamX(1.0), 12));
};
```

### 38-minimap-and-viewport

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo38MinimapViewport
// displayName: Minimap and Viewport
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: One world, two views at once - the camera follows a rover, a minimap shows where it is
// ---

// INTENT: Stage & camera, lesson three: a world can be shown TWICE in the
// same frame:
//
//   DrawSurface(world, cam)   the main view - a camera following the rover.
//   DrawSurfaceRegion         the same world scaled into a corner: a minimap.
//                             No second scene, no duplicate drawing - just a
//                             second way of showing the surface.
//   WorldToScreen             would place overlays in the main view; on the
//                             minimap the mapping is a simple scale, done by
//                             hand in two lines.
//
// The rover wanders a cave world; the minimap frame shows which part of the
// world the camera currently sees.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

const int worldW = 72;
const int worldH = 48;

var world = new BakedSurface(worldW, worldH);
var roverX = 20.0;
var roverY = 24.0;
var clock = new FrameClock();

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var dt = clock.Delta(ctx);

    world.Ensure("cave", s =>
    {
        for (var y = 0; y < worldH; y++)
        for (var x = 0; x < worldW; x++)
        {
            var rock = Noise.Fbm(x * 0.10, y * 0.10, 3) > 0.58;
            s[x, y] = rock
                ? ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.13, 0.20), Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.24, 0.34), Noise.Fbm(x * 0.3, y * 0.3, 2))
                : ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.04, 0.08), Color.FromRgb(0.06, 0.08, 0.13), Noise.Fbm(x * 0.2 + 40, y * 0.2, 2));
        }
        for (var i = 0; i < 30; i++)
        {
            var gx = Hash.From2D(i, 11.0) * worldW;
            var gy = Hash.From2D(i, 12.0) * worldH;
            if (Noise.Fbm(gx * 0.10, gy * 0.10, 3) <= 0.58)
                s.PlotAA(gx, gy, Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.75, 0.65), 0.5);
        }
    });

    // The rover wanders; the clamp keeps the FOLLOW CAMERA inside the world,
    // so the main view never shows the void beyond the edges.
    var (wx, wy) = Steering.Wander(t, seed: 9.0, speed: 0.13);
    roverX = MathH.Clamp(roverX + wx * 7.0 * dt, 12, worldW - 12);
    roverY = MathH.Clamp(roverY + wy * 7.0 * dt, 12, worldH - 12);

    // MAIN VIEW: the camera follows the rover.
    var cam = Camera2D.Focus(roverX, roverY, zoom: 1.0);
    ctx.DrawBackground(Colors.Black);
    ctx.DrawSurface(world.Surface, cam);
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(12, 12, 1.1, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.80, 0.30));

    // MINIMAP: the whole world in the corner - 18x12 pixels, scrimmed.
    const double mapW = 18.0, mapH = 12.0, mapX = 5.0, mapY = 0.0;
    ctx.DrawScrim(mapY, mapH + 1, strength: 0.35);
    ctx.DrawSurfaceRegion(world.Surface, 0, 0, worldW, worldH, mapX, mapY, mapW, mapH, alpha: 0.9);

    // The viewport rectangle and the rover dot, mapped by plain scaling.
    var vx = mapX + (roverX - 12.0) / worldW * mapW;
    var vy = mapY + (roverY - 12.0) / worldH * mapH;
    ctx.DrawRectXyWh(vx, vy, 24.0 / worldW * mapW, 24.0 / worldH * mapH,
        colorStroke: Colors.White.WithAlpha(0.55), strokeWidth: 1, isAntialias: false);
    ctx.SetPixelSafe((int)(mapX + roverX / worldW * mapW), (int)(mapY + roverY / worldH * mapH),
        Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.80, 0.30));
};
```

### 39-rotating-stage

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo39RotatingStage
// displayName: Rotating Stage
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: The camera rotates and breathes over a baked ornament - motion without redrawing a thing
// ---

// INTENT: Stage & camera, lesson four: ROTATION belongs to the camera, not
// the content. An ornament is baked once; every frame only the camera turns
// and breathes:
//
//   Camera2D.Rotation   spins the whole stage under the lens.
//   Camera2D.Zoom       breathes on a slow sine - the picture never stands
//                       still although nothing is redrawn.
//   BakedSurface        one Ensure call, then blit forever - rotation costs
//                       sampling, not drawing.
//
// A second, counter-rotating camera pass of the SAME surface (drawn additive
// at low alpha) gives a kaleidoscope shimmer for free - two cameras, one bake.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var ornament = new BakedSurface(48, 48);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    ornament.Ensure("mandala", s =>
    {
        s.Clear(Colors.Transparent);
        for (var ring = 0; ring < 4; ring++)
        {
            var r = 6.0 + ring * 5.0;
            var count = 6 + ring * 4;
            var col = Palettes.Sunset.Sample(ring / 3.0);
            for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
            {
                var a = i / (double)count * Math.PI * 2.0;
                var x = 24.0 + Math.Cos(a) * r;
                var y = 24.0 + Math.Sin(a) * r;
                if (ring % 2 == 0) s.PlotDiscAA(x, y, 1.2, col);
                else s.DrawSparkle(x, y, 0.8, col, diagonal: i % 2 == 0);
            }
        }
        s.DrawGlow(24, 24, 3.5, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.85, 0.45), coreAlpha: 0.9);
    });

    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.03, 0.02, 0.07));

    // Camera one: slow spin, breathing zoom.
    var cam = Camera2D.Focus(24, 24, zoom: 0.9 + Math.Sin(t * 0.5) * 0.25);
    cam.Rotation = t * 18.0;
    ctx.DrawSurface(ornament.Surface, cam, interpolation: Interpolation.Linear);

    // Camera two: same bake, counter-rotating, additive - the shimmer.
    var ghost = Camera2D.Focus(24, 24, zoom: 1.15 - Math.Sin(t * 0.5) * 0.2);
    ghost.Rotation = -t * 11.0;
    ctx.DrawSurface(ornament.Surface, ghost, alpha: 0.30, blendMode: BlendMode.Plus, interpolation: Interpolation.Linear);
};
```

### 40-filters-on-layers

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo40FiltersOnLayers
// displayName: Filters on Layers
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Depth of field on 24 pixels - background blurred, glow bloomed, subject razor sharp
// ---

// INTENT: Filters, lesson two: a filter on the whole canvas grades the
// PICTURE - a filter on a LAYER grades one THING. That difference is depth
// of field:
//
//   background layer   drawn, then Blur(1.2) - instantly reads as "far away".
//   glow layer         lanterns drawn oversized, then Blur + Plus-blend:
//                      light bleeds over the sharp world without erasing it.
//   subject            drawn LAST, unfiltered - razor sharp against the blur.
//   final grade        one gentle Vignette on the canvas ties it together.
//
// The order is the lesson: blur the far, bloom the light, keep the subject
// sharp, grade the whole - four filters, four different scopes.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    // BACKGROUND LAYER: a street of houses - drawn sharp, then blurred.
    var back = ctx.NewLayer();
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    {
        var col = ColorOps.Lerp(Color.FromRgb(0.04, 0.04, 0.10), Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.08, 0.16), y / 23.0);
        for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++) back[x, y] = col;
    }
    for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++)
    {
        var hx = i * 5.0 - 0.5;
        back.DrawRectXyWh(hx, 8 + (i % 2) * 2, 4, 14, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.12, 0.11, 0.18), isAntialias: false);
        back.DrawRectXyWh(hx + 1, 10 + (i % 2) * 2, 1, 2, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.85, 0.70, 0.35), isAntialias: false);
    }
    back.Apply(filter: Filters.Blur(1.2));

    // GLOW LAYER: lantern light, blurred and ADDED - it bleeds, nothing is lost.
    var glow = ctx.NewLayer();
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        glow.PlotDiscAA(4.0 + i * 8.0, 6.5, 1.6, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.75, 0.30));
    glow.Apply(BlendMode.Plus, filter: Filters.Blur(1.6));

    // Lantern posts and heads stay sharp on the canvas.
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++)
    {
        var lx = 4.0 + i * 8.0;
        ctx.DrawTaperedLine(lx, 21, lx, 7, halfWidth: 0.6, taper: 0.1,
            colorLo: Color.FromRgb(0.34, 0.33, 0.40), colorHi: Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.16, 0.20));
        ctx.PlotDiscAA(lx, 6.5, 0.9, Color.FromRgb(1.00, 0.92, 0.60));
    }

    // SUBJECT: a cat walks the wall - the only razor-sharp mover in the frame.
    var span = 40.0;
    var k = (t * 5.0) % (span * 2.0);
    var forward = k < span;
    var cx = forward ? -4.0 + k : 28.0 - (k - span);
    var bob = Math.Sin(t * 8.0) * 0.4;
    ctx.DrawRectXyWh(0, 20, 24, 4, colorFill: Color.FromRgb(0.07, 0.06, 0.09), isAntialias: false);
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(cx, 19.0 + bob, 1.1, Color.FromRgb(0.90, 0.88, 0.95));
    ctx.PlotDiscAA(cx + (forward ? -1.6 : 1.6), 19.6 + bob, 0.8, Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.78, 0.88));
    ctx.PlotAA(cx + (forward ? -2.8 : 2.8), 18.8 + bob, Color.FromRgb(0.80, 0.78, 0.88), 0.8);

    // FINAL GRADE on the whole canvas - the only full-frame filter.
    ctx.Filter(Filters.Vignette(0.30, 0.95));
};
```

### 41-warp-family

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo41WarpFamily
// displayName: The Warp Family
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Twirl, ripple and field displacement bend one test card - geometry filters, not colour filters
// ---

// INTENT: Filters, lesson three: the WARP family moves PIXELS, not colours.
// One striped test card, three benders, each on its own act:
//
//   Filters.Twirl      angle grows toward the centre - portal, whirlpool.
//                      Animate the strength, not the position.
//   Filters.Ripple     rings run outward from a point - the stone in the pond.
//   Filters.Displace   every pixel shifts where a FIELD points: with
//                      ScalarField.Noise it is heat shimmer; plug in a
//                      WaveField and it is refraction under water.
//
// The card is rebuilt sharp every frame, so each act shows pure filter work -
// nothing else changes between the acts.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var story = new Storyboard(loop: true)
    .Add("twirl", 6.0)
    .Add("ripple", 6.0)
    .Add("shimmer", 6.0);

var shimmer = ScalarField.Noise(scale: 0.35, amplitude: 1.4, driftSpeed: 1.6);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;
    var cue = story.At(ctx);

    // The test card: checkers plus a cross - warps are obvious on it.
    for (var y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (var x = 0; x < 24; x++)
    {
        var check = ((x / 4) + (y / 4)) % 2 == 0;
        ctx[x, y] = check ? Color.FromRgb(0.16, 0.30, 0.45) : Color.FromRgb(0.06, 0.10, 0.18);
    }
    ctx.DrawLine(12, 0, 12, 24, Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.75, 0.30));
    ctx.DrawLine(0, 12, 24, 12, Color.FromRgb(0.95, 0.75, 0.30));
    ctx.DrawCircle(12, 12, 3.2, colorStroke: Colors.White, strokeWidth: 1);

    switch (cue.Name)
    {
        case "twirl":
            // Strength swings; the centre stays put - a portal breathing.
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Twirl(12, 12, strengthDegrees: Math.Sin(cue.LocalSeconds * 1.1) * 160.0, radius: 12.0));
            break;
        case "ripple":
            // Phase runs outward; amplitude fades in and out over the act.
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Ripple(12, 12, wavelength: 5.0,
                amplitude: Envelope.Bell(cue.Progress) * 1.8, phase: cue.LocalSeconds * 5.0));
            break;
        case "shimmer":
            // The same displacement a WaveField would drive - here from noise.
            ctx.Filter(Filters.Displace(shimmer, strengthX: 1.3, strengthY: 0.4, seconds: t));
            break;
    }

    ctx.DrawTextContrastCentered(cue.Name, 1, Fonts.Var3x5, alpha: 0.6);
};
```

### 42-crt-terminal

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo42CrtTerminal
// displayName: CRT Terminal
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: The damage block as a look - phosphor text, scanlines, aberration, and a glitch that strikes on schedule
// ---

// INTENT: Filters, lesson four: DAMAGE is a style. A calm phosphor terminal
// wears a permanent CRT costume, and a real glitch strikes only on schedule:
//
//   permanent costume    Scanlines + RollingScanline + Grain + Vignette,
//                        chained ONCE per frame - the look of glass and dust.
//   scheduled damage     Slots decides when; during the burst the chain gains
//                        ChromaticAberration + Glitch, and the text jumps.
//   phosphor content     Typewriter text in Palettes.Phosphor green with a
//                        TrailBuffer afterglow - the content itself is calm.
//
// Costume always, damage rarely - that contrast is what sells the look.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

var lines = new[] { "PXL OS 1.0", "BOOT... OK", "NET..... OK", "CLOCK... OK", "READY_" };
var trail = new TrailBuffer(24, 24, decay: 0.55);

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds;

    ctx.DrawBackground(Color.FromRgb(0.01, 0.04, 0.02));

    // Phosphor content: lines type themselves, then the cycle restarts.
    var cycle = t % 16.0;
    for (var i = 0; i < lines.Length; i++)
    {
        var start = i * 2.2;
        if (cycle < start) break;
        var text = TextMotion.Typewriter(lines[i], cycle - start, charsPerSecond: 9.0, cursor: i == lines.Length - 1);
        ctx.DrawTextVar3x5(text, 1, 1 + i * 4, Palettes.Phosphor.Sample(0.85));
    }

    // Afterglow: the trail remembers what the screen showed a moment ago.
    trail.Decay();
    ctx.DrawSurface(trail.Surface, blendMode: BlendMode.Plus, alpha: 0.30);
    trail.Capture(ctx, 0.5);

    // The permanent costume - chained once.
    ctx.Filter(Filters.Chain(
        Filters.Scanlines(0.22),
        Filters.RollingScanline((t * 0.30) % 1.0, 4.0, 0.10),
        Filters.Grain(seed: t, strength: 0.05),
        Filters.Vignette(0.35, 0.95)));

    // Scheduled damage: a glitch burst a few times a minute, never randomly.
    var hit = Slots.Progress(t, slotSeconds: 6.0, chance: 0.6, duration: 0.45, seed: 8.0);
    if (hit >= 0)
    {
        var k = Envelope.Spike(hit, power: 2.0);
        ctx.Filter(Filters.Chain(
            Filters.ChromaticAberration(1.0 + k * 1.5),
            Filters.Glitch(seed: Slots.Index(t, 6.0), intensity: 0.25 + k * 0.55)));
    }
};
```

### 43-parameters

```csharp
// ---
// app: LlmDemo43Parameters
// displayName: Parameters
// author: Cumin & Potato
// description: Every knob kind at once - the viewer turns them while the scene keeps running
// ---

// INTENT: Make a pixogram tweakable. A top-level variable initialised with Param.*
// becomes a knob in the PXL app and in the Studio preview:
//
//   Param.Float / Param.Int    a slider with a range
//   Param.Bool                 a switch
//   Param.Color                a colour picker
//   Param.Choice               one of a fixed set of named states
//   Param.Enum<T>              the same, but typed by an enum from this file
//
// The variable name IS the parameter name; label only changes what the viewer reads.
// A new value lands on the NEXT frame - no recompile, no restart, the clock keeps ticking.
//
// The rule that matters: only the parameter variable is live. Anything computed FROM
// it at the file root is computed once, so read it inside the scene lambda.

#:package Pxl@*

using Pxl.Ui.CSharp;

enum Mood
{
    Calm,
    Lively,
    Wild,
}

var speed = Param.Float(1.0, min: 0.1, max: 4.0, label: "Speed");
var ringCount = Param.Int(3, min: 1, max: 6, label: "Rings");
var trails = Param.Bool(true, label: "Trails");
var tint = Param.Color(Colors.Cyan, label: "Tint");
var mood = Param.Enum<Mood>(Mood.Lively, label: "Mood");

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    // Trails: instead of clearing, lay a translucent black over the previous frame.
    ctx.DrawBackground(trails ? Colors.Black.WithAlpha01(0.28) : Colors.Black);

    var wobble = mood switch
    {
        Mood.Calm => 0.0,
        Mood.Lively => 1.6,
        _ => 4.0,
    };

    var t = ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds * speed;

    for (var i = 0; i < ringCount; i++)
    {
        var phase = t + i * 0.7;
        var radius = 3.0 + i * 2.6 + Math.Sin(phase) * (0.8 + wobble * 0.4);
        var drift = Math.Sin(phase * 0.6) * wobble;
        var fade = 1.0 - i / (double)(ringCount + 1);
        ctx.DrawCircle(11.5 + drift, 11.5, radius, colorStroke: tint.WithAlpha01(fade));
    }
};
```

<!-- LLM-EXAMPLES:END -->

---

## API Reference

The sections below document the full `Pxl.Ui.CSharp` drawing API. For exact signatures, parameter docs, and overloads, also see the **XML API Reference** block at the bottom of this document.

### RasterSurface (ctx)

The main entry point for all rendering. Passed as the scene parameter.

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `Width` | int | Canvas width (always 24). Beware: `Width / 2` is integer division |
| `Height` | int | Canvas height (always 24) |
| `WidthF` | double | Canvas width as double (24.0) - use in fractional math |
| `HeightF` | double | Canvas height as double (24.0) |
| `Now` | DateTime | Current local date/time |
| `CycleNo` | long | Current frame number |
| `Elapsed` | TimeSpan | Time since scene start |
| `Fps` | int | Frames per second (~40) |
| `Pixels` | PixelsAccess | Direct pixel read/write access |

### Drawing Methods

All drawing methods are extension methods on `RasterSurface`.

#### Background

```csharp
ctx.DrawBackground(Paint color, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Fills the entire canvas. Default is anti-aliased.

#### Rectangle

```csharp
// By position + size
ctx.DrawRectXyWh(
    double x, double y, double width, double height,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)

// By two corners
ctx.DrawRectXyXy(
    double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

#### Circle

```csharp
ctx.DrawCircle(
    double centerX, double centerY, double radius,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

If neither `colorFill` nor `colorStroke` is specified, defaults to `Colors.Lime` fill.

#### Line

```csharp
ctx.DrawLine(
    double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2,
    Paint? color = null, double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Defaults to `Colors.Lime` if color is null.

#### Point (single pixel)

```csharp
ctx.DrawPoint(
    double x, double y,
    Paint? color = null, double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Defaults to `Colors.Lime` if color is null.

#### Arc (pie slice)

```csharp
// By bounding rectangle
ctx.DrawArc(
    double x, double y, double width, double height,
    double startAngle, double sweepAngle,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)

// By center point
ctx.DrawArcCenter(
    double centerX, double centerY, double radius,
    double startAngle, double sweepAngle,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Angles: 0 = right, 90 = down. Positive sweep = clockwise.

#### Triangle

```csharp
ctx.DrawTriangle(
    double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2, double x3, double y3,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Filled or stroked triangle defined by three corner points.

#### Polygon / Polyline

```csharp
ctx.DrawPolygon(
    (double X, double Y)[] points,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)

ctx.DrawPolyline(
    (double X, double Y)[] points,
    Paint? color = null, double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

`DrawPolygon` closes back to the first point automatically. `DrawPolyline` is open (stroke only, no fill).

#### Ellipse

```csharp
ctx.DrawEllipse(
    double centerX, double centerY,
    double radiusX, double radiusY,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

For a circle, use `DrawCircle` instead.

#### Rounded Rectangle

```csharp
ctx.DrawRoundedRect(
    double x, double y, double width, double height,
    double cornerRadius,
    Paint? colorFill = null, Paint? colorStroke = null,
    double strokeWidth = 1, bool isAntialias = true)
```

Uniform `cornerRadius` for all four corners.

### Text

#### Drawing Text

```csharp
// Generic (defaults to Var4x5 font, White color, isAntialias = false)
ctx.DrawText(
    string text, double x, double y,
    FontInfo? font = null, Paint? color = null, double? fontSize = null,
    bool isAntialias = false)

// Font-specific convenience methods (all default isAntialias = false for crisp pixels)
ctx.DrawTextVar3x5(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono3x5(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextVar4x5(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono4x5(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono6x6(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono7x10(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextVar10x10(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono10x10(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
ctx.DrawTextMono16x16(text, x, y, color: Colors.White)
```

#### Layout Helpers

```csharp
// Centered horizontally on the canvas
ctx.DrawTextCentered(text, y, font: Fonts.Var4x5, color: Colors.White);

// Aligned around an anchor (horizontal only)
ctx.DrawTextAligned(text, anchorX, y, TextAlign.Centre, font, color);

// Aligned around an anchor (horizontal + vertical)
ctx.DrawTextAligned(text, anchorX, anchorY,
    TextAlign.Right, VerticalAlign.Bottom, font, color);

// Positioned + clipped inside a rectangle
ctx.DrawTextInRect(text, x: 0, y: 18, width: 24, height: 5,
    hAlign: TextAlign.Centre, vAlign: VerticalAlign.Middle,
    font: Fonts.Mono4x5, color: Colors.White);

// Marquee — scrolls the text right-to-left, wrapping with a gap
ctx.DrawMarquee("Hello PXL Clock — long title that doesn't fit",
    x: 0, y: 19, width: 24, height: 5,
    pixelsPerSecond: 6.0, gapPixels: 4.0,
    font: Fonts.Mono4x5, color: Colors.White);
```

Enums:
- `TextAlign`: `Left | Centre | Right`
- `VerticalAlign`: `Top | Middle | Bottom`

#### Edging and Hinting

For pixel-perfect rendering keep the defaults. To soften edges or align glyphs more aggressively:

```csharp
ctx.DrawText(
    text, x, y,
    edging: TextEdging.AntiAlias,           // Pixel (default) | AntiAlias | SubpixelAntiAlias
    hinting: TextHinting.Slight             // None (default) | Slight | Normal | Full
);
```

#### Measuring Text

```csharp
double width  = ctx.MeasureText(text, font, fontSize);
double height = ctx.MeasureTextHeight(font, fontSize);

// Font-specific width variants
double w = ctx.MeasureTextVar3x5(text);
double w2 = ctx.MeasureTextMono4x5(text);
// ... (same pattern for all fonts)
```

#### Available Fonts

| Font | Style | Approx Size | Best For |
|------|-------|-------------|----------|
| `Fonts.Var3x5` | Proportional | 3x5 px | Compact text, labels |
| `Fonts.Mono3x5` | Monospace | 3x5 px | Compact aligned text |
| `Fonts.Var4x5` | Proportional | 4x5 px | Default text (good readability) |
| `Fonts.Mono4x5` | Monospace | 4x5 px | Time display, counters |
| `Fonts.Mono6x6` | Monospace | 6x6 px | Medium text |
| `Fonts.Mono7x10` | Monospace | 7x10 px | Large text |
| `Fonts.Var10x10` | Proportional | 10x10 px | Headlines |
| `Fonts.Mono10x10` | Monospace | 10x10 px | Large aligned text |
| `Fonts.Mono16x16` | Monospace | 16x16 px | Very large text (1-2 chars) |
| `Fonts.AdafruitTomThumb` | Proportional bitmap | 3x5 px | Tiny labels, pixel-exact (no rasterizer) |
| `Fonts.AdafruitPicopixel` | Proportional bitmap | ~3x6 px | Tiny text, pixel-exact |
| `Fonts.AdafruitOrg01` | Monospace bitmap | ~4x5 px | Techy look, pixel-exact |
| `Fonts.AdafruitClassic` | Monospace bitmap | 5x7 px | Retro terminal look, pixel-exact |

The four Adafruit fonts are bitmap fonts: glyphs are blitted pixel-exact with no
rasterizer, so they never anti-alias. A hand-authored `PixelFont` can join this
family via `pixelFont.ToFontInfo()` and then works with every `DrawText*` helper.

### Colors

#### Color Struct

```csharp
// Constructor (double 0.0-1.0)
new Color(double r, double g, double b, double a = 1.0)

// Factory methods (double 0.0-1.0)
Color.FromRgb(r, g, b)
Color.FromRgba(r, g, b, a)
Color.FromArgb(a, r, g, b)
Color.FromHsl(hue, saturation, lightness)        // all 0.0-1.0
Color.FromHsl360(hue, saturation, lightness)     // hue 0-360, rest 0.0-1.0
Color.FromHsv(hue, saturation, value)            // all 0.0-1.0
Color.FromHsv360(hue, saturation, value)         // hue 0-360, rest 0.0-1.0

// Factory methods (byte 0-255)
Color.FromRgbByte(r, g, b)
Color.FromRgbaByte(r, g, b, a)
Color.FromArgbByte(a, r, g, b)

// Hex string (3, 4, 6, or 8 chars; '#' optional; case-insensitive)
Color.FromHex("#FF8800")        // RRGGBB
Color.FromHex("F80")            // RGB short
Color.FromHex("#FF8800CC")      // RRGGBBAA

// Modifiers (return new Color)
color.WithAlpha(double alpha)       // 0.0-1.0
color.WithAlphaByte(byte alpha)     // 0-255

// Properties
color.R, color.G, color.B, color.A             // double 0.0-1.0
color.RedByte, color.GreenByte, color.BlueByte, color.AlphaByte  // byte 0-255
```

#### Color Operations (ColorOps)

Operations BETWEEN colours, in addition to the constructors above:

```csharp
// Componentwise linear interpolation. t is clamped to [0, 1].
Color mid = ColorOps.Lerp(Colors.Red, Colors.Blue, 0.5);
Color mid2 = Colors.Red.LerpTo(Colors.Blue, 0.5);

// Mix this colour TOWARD another by `strength` (0..1).
// Useful for "warm horizon tint" or "fade in ambient".
Color tinted = waterColor.Tinted(Colors.Orange, 0.3);

// Multiplicative lighting: simulate `color × light × brightness`,
// clamped per channel. For tinting objects under colored light.
Color litWood = woodColor.LitBy(moonlightColor, 0.4);

// N-way weighted blend (weights normalised internally)
Color sky = ColorOps.Blend(
    new[] { dawnSky, noonSky, duskSky },
    new[] { dawnWeight, noonWeight, duskWeight });
```

#### Palettes (colour-over-time / value-mapped lookups)

A `Palette` is an ordered set of colour stops sampled by a normalised position t ∈ [0, 1]. Use it for time-of-day tints, heatmaps, value-mapped colour lookups, fire/lava/ice effects.

```csharp
// Custom palette with evenly-spaced stops
var p = new Palette(Colors.Black, Colors.Red, Colors.Yellow, Colors.White);
Color c = p.Sample(0.5);                       // half way → orange-yellow
Color c2 = p.SampleWrapped(t);                 // wraps t into [0, 1] (periodic)

// Custom palette with explicit stops
var p2 = new Palette(
    new[] { Colors.Black, Colors.Red, Colors.White },
    new[] { 0.0, 0.7, 1.0 });

// Built-in palettes
Palettes.Rainbow      // full spectrum
Palettes.Heat         // cool blue → green → yellow → red
Palettes.Fire         // black → red → orange → yellow → white
Palettes.Ice          // deep blue → ice blue → frosted white
Palettes.Sunset       // violet → magenta → orange → gold → pale yellow
Palettes.Grayscale    // black → white
Palettes.Phosphor     // CRT green
```

#### Predefined Colors (Colors class)

Common colors: `Colors.Black`, `Colors.White`, `Colors.Red`, `Colors.Green`, `Colors.Blue`, `Colors.Yellow`, `Colors.Cyan`, `Colors.Magenta`, `Colors.Orange`, `Colors.Purple`, `Colors.Pink`, `Colors.Lime`, `Colors.Gold`, `Colors.Silver`, `Colors.Gray`, `Colors.DarkBlue`, `Colors.DarkRed`, `Colors.DarkGreen`, `Colors.Coral`, `Colors.Crimson`, `Colors.DeepPink`, `Colors.DeepSkyBlue`, `Colors.DodgerBlue`, `Colors.Tomato`, `Colors.Turquoise`, `Colors.Violet`

Special: `Colors.TransparentBlack`, `Colors.TransparentWhite`

140+ named colors are available (standard CSS/X11 color names).

### Paints (Advanced Fills)

Colors are implicitly converted to solid paints. For gradients/patterns, use the `Paints` factory:

```csharp
// Solid color (implicit via Color)
ctx.DrawCircle(12, 12, 5, colorFill: Colors.Red);

// Linear gradient
Paints.LinearGradient((0, 0), (24, 0), new[] { Colors.Red, Colors.Blue })
Paints.VerticalGradient(24, Colors.Red, Colors.Blue)
Paints.HorizontalGradient(24, Colors.Red, Colors.Blue)

// Radial gradient
Paints.RadialGradient((12, 12), 10, new[] { Colors.White, Colors.Black })

// Two-point conical (cone gradient between two circles)
Paints.TwoPointConicalGradient((6, 6), 1, (18, 18), 8, new[] { Colors.White, Colors.Blue })

// Sweep (angular) gradient
Paints.SweepGradient((12, 12), new[] { Colors.Red, Colors.Green, Colors.Blue })

// Image pattern (tiles a SingleImage as a fill)
var img = Image.LoadSingleImage("assets/tile.png");
Paints.ImagePattern(img, tileX: TileMode.Repeat, tileY: TileMode.Mirror)

// Perlin noise (static — for animation, animate the seed or sample coords yourself)
Paints.PerlinNoiseFractal(0.1, 0.1, 4, 42)
Paints.PerlinNoiseTurbulence(0.1, 0.1, 4, 42)
```

#### TileMode

Gradient and image-pattern paints accept a `TileMode` to control behaviour outside the primary domain:

- `TileMode.Clamp` — repeat the edge color (default for gradients)
- `TileMode.Repeat` — tile the pattern, repeating end to start
- `TileMode.Mirror` — tile the pattern, mirroring every other repetition
- `TileMode.Decal` — render only inside the primary domain; outside is transparent

```csharp
Paints.LinearGradient((0, 0), (8, 0), new[] { Colors.Red, Colors.Blue }, tileMode: TileMode.Mirror);
```

#### Transform2D

`SweepGradient` and `ImagePattern` accept an optional `Transform2D` (an affine 2D transform — translation, scale, rotation, skew) to position/orient the paint:

```csharp
var t = Transform2D.Translate(2, 0).Then(Transform2D.Rotate(45, 12, 12));
Paints.SweepGradient((12, 12), colors, localTransform: t);
```

Available factories: `Transform2D.Identity`, `Translate(dx, dy)`, `Scale(s)` / `Scale(sx, sy)`, `Rotate(degrees)` / `Rotate(degrees, pivotX, pivotY)`, `Skew(kx, ky)`. Compose left-to-right with `.Then(other)`.

> **Note on Perlin noise:** the methods take fixed parameters and return a static noise field. They do not animate on their own. To create motion, use `Paints.PerlinNoiseFractal(baseFreqX, baseFreqY, octaves, (int)(ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds * 100))` — i.e. drive the seed from elapsed time.

### Animations

#### Value Animations

Create animations outside the scene, call `.Eval(ctx)` inside.
The `Animate` factory class and `Repeat` enum are in `Pxl.Ui.CSharp`. The returned `Animation`/`ToggleAnimation` types live in `Pxl.Ui.CSharp.Animations` — use `var` and you won't need an extra `using`.

```csharp
// Create (outside scene)
var anim = Animate.Linear(durationSeconds, startValue, endValue,
    repeat: Repeat.Once, autoStart: true);

// Available easings
Animate.Linear(...)
Animate.EaseIn(...)        // Quadratic: slow start
Animate.EaseOut(...)       // Quadratic: slow end
Animate.EaseInOut(...)     // Quadratic: slow start & end
Animate.EaseInSine(...)
Animate.EaseOutSine(...)
Animate.EaseInOutSine(...)
Animate.EaseInCubic(...)
Animate.EaseOutCubic(...)
Animate.EaseInOutCubic(...)
Animate.Custom(easingFn, ...)  // Custom easing: Func<double, double> (0..1 -> 0..1)

// Use in scene
var x = anim.Eval(ctx);  // Returns current double value (cached per frame)

// Properties
anim.Value      // double: current cached value
anim.ValueInt   // int: current value as integer
anim.IsRunning  // bool
anim.IsAtEnd    // bool (Repeat.Once only)

// Control
anim.Pause();
anim.Resume();
anim.Restart();
```

#### Repeat Modes

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `Repeat.Once` | Play once, stop at end value |
| `Repeat.Loop` | Restart from beginning each cycle |
| `Repeat.PingPong` | Alternate forward and reverse |

#### Toggle Animation

Cycles through discrete values at intervals:

```csharp
var toggle = Animate.ToggleValues(intervalSeconds, value1, value2, value3, ...);

// In scene:
var current = toggle.Eval(ctx);  // Returns current T value
```

#### Periodic helpers (stateless)

For simple recurring motion (bobbing, orbits, drift) you don't need a stateful animation object — just sample directly from `ctx.Elapsed`:

```csharp
// Sinusoidal oscillation: amplitude * sin(2π * elapsed / periodSeconds + phaseOffset)
var bob = Animate.Sine(ctx, periodSeconds: 2.0, amplitude: 1.5);
ctx.DrawCircle(12, 12 + bob, 3, colorFill: Colors.Cyan);

// 2D orbit on an ellipse
var (sunX, sunY) = Animate.Orbit(ctx,
    periodSeconds: 24.0,
    centerX: 12, centerY: 10,
    radiusX: 7,  radiusY: 12,
    phaseOffset: 0);
```

Both are pure functions of `ctx.Elapsed` — safe to call multiple times per frame, no caching needed, no state.

### Images

#### Static Images

```csharp
// Load (outside scene) — paths relative to script file
var img = Image.LoadSingleImage("assets/myimage.png");

// Transform (returns new instance, immutable)
var resized = img.Resize(24, 24, useAntiAlias: false);
var cropped = img.Crop(left: 2, top: 2, right: 2, bottom: 2);
var region = img.CropRegion(x: 0, y: 0, width: 16, height: 16);

// Draw (inside scene)
ctx.DrawImage(img, x, y);

// Draw scaled to a destination size
ctx.DrawImage(img, x, y, width, height,
    interpolation: Interpolation.NearestNeighbor);  // or Linear

// Draw a SOURCE REGION of the image into a destination rectangle
ctx.DrawImageRegion(img,
    srcX, srcY, srcWidth, srcHeight,
    dstX, dstY, dstWidth, dstHeight,
    interpolation: Interpolation.NearestNeighbor);

// Draw rotated around an arbitrary pivot point
ctx.DrawImageRotated(img, x, y,
    rotationDegrees: 30,
    pivotX: 12, pivotY: 12);

// All DrawImage overloads support optional opacity + blendMode
ctx.DrawImage(img, x, y,
    opacity: 0.5,                          // 0..1
    blendMode: BlendMode.Plus);            // additive glow, multiply, etc.
```

#### Animated GIFs

```csharp
// Load
var gif = Image.LoadAnimatedGif("assets/animation.gif");

// Transform
var resized = gif.Resize(24, 24);
var cropped = gif.Crop(left: 2, top: 2);
var region = gif.CropRegion(0, 0, 20, 20);
var slowed = gif.WithFrameDuration(200);  // ms per frame

// Draw (auto-animates based on ctx.Elapsed)
ctx.DrawImage(gif, x, y, repeat: true);

// Properties
gif.FrameCount, gif.Width, gif.Height, gif.TotalDuration
```

#### Sprite Maps

```csharp
// Create from image
var sheet = Image.LoadSingleImage("assets/spritesheet.png");
var sprites = sheet.ToSpriteMap(cellWidth: 16, cellHeight: 16, frameDurationMs: 100);

// Access cells
var cell = sprites[row, col];  // Returns SingleImage

// Create animation from cells
var walkAnim = sprites.CreateAnimation((0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3));
ctx.DrawImage(walkAnim, x, y);

// Properties
sprites.Rows, sprites.Columns, sprites.CellWidth, sprites.CellHeight
```

### Direct Pixel Access

```csharp
// Single pixel — caller must ensure (x, y) are inside the canvas
ctx.SetPixel(x, y, color);
Color c = ctx.GetPixel(x, y);

// Bounds-safe variants — silently ignore out-of-canvas reads/writes
ctx.SetPixelSafe(x, y, color);              // no-op if (x,y) is outside
bool ok = ctx.TrySetPixel(x, y, color);     // returns false if outside
Color c2 = ctx.GetPixelOrDefault(x, y, fallback: Colors.Black);
bool got = ctx.TryGetPixel(x, y, out var c3);
bool inside = ctx.IsInBounds(x, y);

// Use the safe variants in any per-pixel pass that might generate
// coordinates near the edges (drift, rotation, sub-pixel jitter, etc.).

// Via Pixels property
var pixels = ctx.Pixels;
pixels[x, y] = Colors.Red;          // 2D access
Color c = pixels[x, y];
pixels[index] = Colors.Blue;        // Linear index (row-major: index = y * 24 + x)

// Iterate every pixel with coordinates
foreach (var cell in ctx.Pixels.Cells)
{
    // cell.X, cell.Y are int; cell.Color is Color
    var dist = Math.Sqrt((cell.X - 12) * (cell.X - 12) + (cell.Y - 12) * (cell.Y - 12));
    pixels[cell.X, cell.Y] = Colors.White.WithAlpha(1.0 - dist / 17.0);
}

// Bulk write — colorArray is a 1D array of length Width * Height (576) in row-major order
Color[] buffer = new Color[24 * 24];
for (int y = 0; y < 24; y++)
    for (int x = 0; x < 24; x++)
        buffer[y * 24 + x] = Color.FromHsl((x + y) / 48.0, 1.0, 0.5);
ctx.SetPixels(buffer, BlendMode.Source);
```

### Layers (Fork / NewLayer)

```csharp
// Fork: copies current canvas state into a new layer
var layer = ctx.Fork();
layer.DrawCircle(12, 12, 8, colorFill: Colors.Red);
layer.Apply(BlendMode.SourceOver);

// NewLayer: blank canvas
var layer = ctx.NewLayer(clearColor: Colors.Transparent);
layer.DrawCircle(12, 12, 8, colorFill: Colors.Yellow);
layer.Apply(BlendMode.Screen);

// A layer can be BIGGER than the canvas — paint at a higher resolution and
// scale it down, or scroll a wide layer across the canvas.
var wide = ctx.NewLayer(Colors.Transparent, width: 72, height: 24);
wide.DrawTextMono6x6("SCROLLING", 0, 9, color: Colors.White);
wide.Translate(-offset, 0);
wide.Apply();

// Apply can run a filter on the layer right before compositing
layer.Apply(BlendMode.Plus, filter: Filters.Blur(1.5));
```

#### Layer Transforms

Transforms accumulate on the layer and are applied automatically when calling `Apply()`:

```csharp
var layer = ctx.NewLayer(clearColor: Colors.Transparent);
layer.DrawCircle(12, 12, 5, colorFill: Colors.Red);

// Transforms (call order matters — they accumulate)
layer.Scale(2.0);                    // uniform scale
layer.Scale(2.0, 1.5);               // non-uniform scale
layer.Translate(5, 3);               // move
layer.Rotate(45);                    // rotate around layer center (degrees)
layer.Rotate(45, 12, 12);            // rotate around specific point (x, y)

// Or use a Transform2D (same type used by paints) — useful when composing transforms
var t = Transform2D.Translate(5, 3).Then(Transform2D.Rotate(45, 12, 12));
layer.SetTransform(t);               // replaces the accumulated transform
layer.ApplyTransform(t);             // composes on top of existing

// Apply with blend mode and interpolation
layer.Apply(
    BlendMode.SourceOver,            // default: SourceOver
    Interpolation.NearestNeighbor);  // default: NearestNeighbor (sharp pixels)
```

#### Interpolation Modes

| Value | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `Interpolation.NearestNeighbor` | Sharp, blocky pixels (default — ideal for pixel art) |
| `Interpolation.Linear` | Smooth, bilinear interpolation |

#### Common Blend Modes

| Mode | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `BlendMode.SourceOver` | Standard alpha blending (default) |
| `BlendMode.Screen` | Lighten (additive-like) |
| `BlendMode.Multiply` | Darken |
| `BlendMode.Plus` | Add colors (clamp to white) — most common for "glow" effects |
| `BlendMode.Source` | Replace destination |
| `BlendMode.SourceIn` | Mask source by destination alpha |
| `BlendMode.SourceOut` | Inverse mask |
| `BlendMode.Xor` | XOR |

### Math & Hash Helpers

```csharp
// Math (static class MathH)
MathH.Clamp01(v)                       // clamp to [0, 1]
MathH.Clamp(v, min, max)               // clamp to [min, max]
MathH.Lerp(a, b, t)                    // linear interpolation, t can be outside [0,1]
MathH.LerpClamped(a, b, t)             // same, clamped
MathH.Smoothstep(t)                    // t² * (3 - 2t), clamped
MathH.Smootherstep(t)                  // 6t⁵ - 15t⁴ + 10t³, clamped (Perlin's smoother curve)
MathH.Remap(v, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)         // linear remap, NOT clamped
MathH.RemapClamped(v, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)  // linear remap, output-clamped

// Pseudo-random hash (static class Hash) — deterministic, no state
double r = Hash.From2D(x, y);          // 2D position → [0, 1)
double r = Hash.From3D(x, y, z);       // 3D, e.g. with time slice
double r = Hash.From1D(v);             // single index
```

Both classes are pure functional helpers — same input always returns the same output. Use `Hash.From2D` for procedural placement (stars, foam scatter, glitter spots) where you want stability across frames.

### Offscreen Surfaces & Camera

Paint a world that is larger than the canvas, then show a part of it. This is
how zoom, pan and "bake the expensive part once" work.

```csharp
// An offscreen surface of ANY size that shares ctx's time (Elapsed, Now, CycleNo)
var world = ctx.CreateSurface(200, 120);
world.DrawCircle(100, 60, 20, colorFill: Colors.Teal);

// A camera decides which part of the world the 24x24 canvas shows.
// Zoom = canvas pixels per world pixel: 1 = 1:1, 4 = magnified, 0.25 = overview.
var cam = Camera2D.Focus(centerX: 100, centerY: 60, zoom: 3.0);
cam.Rotation = 15;                                   // degrees, optional
ctx.DrawSurface(world, cam);                         // pan/zoom/rotate in one call
ctx.DrawSurface(world, cam, alpha: 0.8, blendMode: BlendMode.SourceOver,
                interpolation: Interpolation.NearestNeighbor);

// Smooth camera moves: LerpTo interpolates zoom geometrically, so a zoom-in
// feels linear at every scale.
var shot = Camera2D.Focus(20, 20, 0.25).LerpTo(Camera2D.Focus(80, 40, 4.0), u);

// World <-> screen, e.g. to place an overlay on a world object
var (sx, sy) = cam.WorldToScreen(wx, wy, ctx.Width, ctx.Height);

// Plain composition without a camera
ctx.DrawSurface(other, x: 4, y: 2, alpha: 0.5);      // 1:1 blit
ctx.DrawSurfaceRegion(world, srcX: 40, srcY: 20, srcWidth: 24, srcHeight: 24);
var copy = ctx.Snapshot();                           // detached copy of the canvas
```

**Baking** — render expensive static content ONCE and blit it afterwards. Declare
the `BakedSurface` outside the scene lambda; `Ensure` re-renders only when the key
changes:

```csharp
var backdrop = new BakedSurface(24, 24);             // outside scene

var scene = (RasterSurface ctx) =>
{
    backdrop.Ensure(variantIndex, s => PaintBackdrop(s, variantIndex));
    ctx.DrawSurface(backdrop.Surface);
};
```

### Filters

Post-processing over a whole surface. Filters are meant to run on an isolated
layer, so an effect stays inside the layer it belongs to.

```csharp
ctx.Filter(Filters.Blur(1.4));                       // in place on the canvas
ctx.Filter(Filters.Vignette(0.5), Filters.Posterize(4));   // several, in order
layer.Apply(BlendMode.Plus, filter: Filters.Blur(2.0));    // filter, then composite
```

| Filter | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `Filters.Blur(radius)` | Gaussian blur, alpha-correct (no black bleeding) |
| `Filters.Sharpen(strength, radius)` | Unsharp mask |
| `Filters.Bloom(threshold, radius, strength)` | Bright areas glow |
| `Filters.EdgeDetect(strength, edgeColor, keepSource)` | Sobel outlines |
| `Filters.ColorGrade(tint, brightness, contrast, saturation)` | Mood in one call |
| `Filters.Levels(inBlack, inWhite, gamma)` | Black/white point, gamma |
| `Filters.Posterize(levels)` | Quantise channels |
| `Filters.Grayscale(amount)` | Desaturate |
| `Filters.Vignette(strength, radius, color)` | Darken toward the edges |
| `Filters.Fade(color, amount)` | Blend everything toward a colour (cuts, fog) |
| `Filters.Glint(position, angleDegrees, width, color, strength, mask)` | Glass sweep; `mask` is a `Mask` confining it to a subject |
| `Filters.Mirror(atY, fade, depth, tint, tintStrength, distortion, distortionStrength, seconds)` | Reflection below a line |
| `Filters.Custom((color, x, y) => newColor)` | Any per-pixel colour filter |
| `Filters.Grain(seed, strength)` | Film grain - flat gradients start to look like material |
| `Filters.ChannelRotate(steps)` | False colour in one line |
| warp / damage | see "Warp, Glitch and CRT" below |
| `Filters.Chain(a, b, c)` | Several filters as one |

`Filters.Mirror` takes an optional `IScalarField` for distortion — pass the same
`WaveField` that ripples the water and the reflection ripples with it.

### Storyboard, Cycles & Stagger

A scene cut into named segments instead of hand-summed time constants.

```csharp
var story = new Storyboard(loop: true, seamFade: 0.4)     // outside scene
    .Add("grow", 5.0)
    .Add("fall", 2.4)
    .Add("hold", 4.5);

var cue = story.At(ctx);
cue.Name          // running segment
cue.Progress      // 0..1 inside that segment
cue.LocalSeconds  // seconds inside that segment
cue.Cycle         // how often the whole storyboard has looped
cue.CycleSeconds  // seconds since the cycle started
cue.SeamFade      // 1 in the middle, ramps to 0 at both cycle borders

if (cue.Is("fall")) DrawFall(ctx, cue.Progress);
story.Progress("grow", ctx);   // 0 before, 0..1 during, 1 after — crosses borders
story.DurationOf("fall");
story.StartOf("fall");

if (cue.SeamFade < 0.999) ctx.Filter(Filters.Fade(Colors.Black, 1.0 - cue.SeamFade));
```

Per-cycle variants without repeating the previous one, and staggered group timing:

```csharp
var picker = new CyclePicker(count: 3);      // outside scene
if (picker.Update(cue.Cycle)) Rebake();      // true exactly when the pick changed
var variant = variants[picker.Current];

Stagger.Progress(index, seconds, duration, delayPerItem);   // item after item
Stagger.Spread(index, count, seconds, totalSeconds, overlap); // group ends together
```

Easing curves are available as plain functions too - `Easings` is the ONE
catalog behind all `Animate` factories (`Linear`, `Smoothstep`, `Smootherstep`,
Quad/Cubic/Sine each as `EaseIn`/`EaseOut`/`EaseInOut*`, `EaseOutBack`,
`EaseInBack`, `EaseOutElastic`, `EaseOutBounce`),
and as animations: `Animate.EaseOutBack(...)`, `Animate.EaseOutElastic(...)`,
`Animate.EaseOutBounce(...)`, `Animate.EaseInBack(...)`.

### Day & Night

One `DayCycle` should drive the whole mood of a scene: sky colours, light,
stars, the clock overlay. Never re-derive the hour in several places.

```csharp
var cycle = DayCycle.FromClock(ctx);                  // real time of day
var cycle = DayCycle.Animated(ctx, secondsPerDay: 24);// fast-forward for previews
var cycle = DayCycle.Fixed(18.5);                     // freeze one moment

cycle.Hour, cycle.Progress, cycle.Phase, cycle.Sun
cycle.Day, cycle.Night, cycle.Twilight                // eased factors, 0..1
```

Sun and moon travel elliptic arcs; a moon is just a body with `PhaseOffset = PI`:

```csharp
var sun  = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = horizonY, AmpX = 9,  AmpY = 13 };
var moon = new SkyBody { CenterX = 12, CenterY = horizonY, AmpX = 13, AmpY = 7,
                         PhaseOffset = Math.PI };

var s = sun.At(cycle);
s.X, s.Y, s.Altitude, s.IsUp
s.Lowness        // 0 high up, 1 at the horizon — drives warm tints and stretch
s.Fade(10.0)     // afterglow: 1 while up, fading over N pixels below the horizon

Moon.Phase(ctx.Now.ToUniversalTime());        // 0 = new, 0.5 = full
Moon.Illumination(...);                       // 0..1 lit fraction
Moon.ShadowOffset(...);                       // -1..1, where to put the shadow disc
```

Ambient light and time-of-day palettes:

```csharp
var light = Lighting.FromAltitude(s, startAltitude: -3, fullAltitude: 9);  // s = sun.At(cycle)
// (an overload also takes a raw double altitude)
light.Ambient;                       // 0..1
light.Tint;                          // warm at dusk, neutral at noon
light.Apply(materialColor);          // colour x tint x ambient
light.Apply(materialColor, minAmbient: 0.1);   // never fully black

var skyTop = new PhasePalette(
    night:    Color.FromRgb(0.02, 0.03, 0.10),
    twilight: Color.FromRgb(0.30, 0.18, 0.42),
    day:      Color.FromRgb(0.35, 0.65, 1.00));
var col = skyTop.Sample(cycle);
```

### Painting a Sky That Reads as a Sky

Deriving the time of day is half the job. The other half is HOW the sky is
painted, and it is where most attempts stay flat. Three mechanisms do the work:

```csharp
// 1) THREE horizon colours instead of one. The warm one is pulled toward the
//    sun's column, the cool one toward the moon's, the far one fills the rest.
var sky = new SkyGradient
{
    HorizonY = 13, PullSpread = 46,          // sigma^2 of the sideways pull
    Top         = new PhasePalette(night, twilight, day),
    Horizon     = new PhasePalette(night, twilight, day),   // away from any body
    SunHorizon  = new PhasePalette(night, twilight, day),   // warm
    MoonHorizon = new PhasePalette(night, twilight, day),   // cool
};
sky.Draw(ctx, cycle, sun.At(cycle), moon.At(cycle));

// The same colour BELOW the line, so the glow does not stop at the horizon:
var waterTop = sky.HorizonColorAt(x + 0.5, cycle, s, m);
```

A single horizon colour gives an even orange wash over the whole sky. The pull
gives a warm COLUMN with cool sky beside it - that contrast is the sunset.

```csharp
// 2) The body is stretched and layered, not a disc.
var sunGlow = SkyGlow.Sun();        // soft gaussian core, strong stretch
var moonGlow = SkyGlow.Moon();      // crisp small disc, wide faint halo
moonGlow.ShadowOffset = Moon.ShadowOffset(ctx.Now.ToUniversalTime()) * 3.2;
moonGlow.Draw(ctx, m, maxY: horizonY, brightness: 0.85);
sunGlow.Draw(ctx, s, maxY: horizonY);
```

`StretchAtHorizon` squashes the ellipse sideways as the body sinks - a round
disc reads as a lamp, a smeared one as light through kilometres of air.
`HighStrength` keeps the glow modest while the body is high. And the core is cut
at the horizon while the glow keeps burning `LingerPixels` below it - **that
split is what an afterglow is**.

```csharp
// 3) On water, the reflection is a PATH of broken light, not a mirrored disc.
var beam = new SpecularBeam { TopY = waterY, Length = 10, WidthBase = 0.8, WidthGrow = 0.55 };
beam.SourceX = s.X;
beam.Draw(ctx, sea, t, beamColor: warm, glowColor: brighter, sparkColor: white,
          intensity: s.Fade(4.0));
```

Three layers - base beam, glow on rising water, sparks on the crests - read as a
path of light; one layer reads as a stripe.

### Depth: Camera, Streaming, Fog

A pinhole camera over a ground plane is the cheapest way to get real depth.
World points are `(wx, wz)`: lateral position and distance from the camera.

```csharp
var cam = new PinholeCamera { Height = 1.6, Focal = 24.0, HorizonY = 10.0, CenterX = 12.0 };

var (sx, sy, scale) = cam.Project(wx, wz);  // screen position + pixels per world unit
cam.DepthAtScreenY(sy);                     // inverse: which depth is this row?
cam.FrustumHalfWidth(wz);                   // how wide is the visible cone there?
cam.IsInFrustum(wx, wz);
```

Objects that travel past the camera and recycle, with edge fades:

```csharp
var stream = new WorldStream { Speed = 1.6, RecycleFrom = -26, RecycleTo = 26, FadeMarginPx = 10 };
var items = new (double Wx0, double Wz)[] { (-20, 21), (-6, 15), (8, 11) };

foreach (var it in stream.Place(items, cam, ctx.Elapsed.TotalSeconds))
{
    it.Wx; it.Wz; it.ScreenX; it.ScreenY; it.Scale;
    it.Visibility;      // 0..1 edge fade, so recycling is never visible
}
```

Painter's order and haze:

```csharp
foreach (var it in Depth.Behind(placed, boatWz)) Draw(it);
DrawBoat();
foreach (var it in Depth.InFront(placed, boatWz)) Draw(it);
foreach (var it in Depth.BackToFront(placed)) Draw(it);

var haze = Fog.Amount(wz, nearZ: 5, farZ: 24, nearHaze: 0.05, farHaze: 0.6);
var col = Fog.Apply(baseColor, haze, horizonColor);
```

### Fields: Waves, Noise, Scatter

A field is a number you can sample anywhere. One field can drive many things at
once — surface colour, foam, reflections, how a boat rolls — and they stay in
sync for free.

```csharp
var sea = new WaveField                       // outside scene
{
    OriginY = horizonY,
    Octaves = 3,
    CrossStrength = 0.35,      // counter-running train, breaks the 1D look
    DomainWarp = 0.45,         // bends the fronts
    PerspectiveSquash = 0.025, // rows compress toward the horizon
    Speed = 1.8,
};

sea.Value(x, y, t);                  // roughly -1.6 .. 1.6
sea.SlopeX(x, y, t);                 // roll angle of a boat
sea.Normal(x, y, t);                 // lighting
sea.Crest(x, y, t, threshold, range);// 0..1 foam / glitter strength
```

```csharp
Noise.Value(x, y);                   // smooth value noise, 0..1
Noise.Value(x, y, z);                // pass time as z
Noise.Fbm(x, y, octaves);            // fractal noise
Noise.Fbm(x, y, t, octaves);         // drifting fractal noise
Noise.Ridged(x, y, octaves);         // sharp crests

Scatter.Has(x, y, density);          // is this pixel part of the scatter?
Scatter.At(x, y, density);           // 0..1 strength, gives brightness spread
Scatter.Value(x, y);                 // stable per-pixel random (phases, hues)
Scatter.Pick(x, y, w0, w1, w2);      // stable weighted choice (star shapes)
```

Anything can BECOME a field. `IScalarField` consumers (`Filters.Mirror`,
`Filters.Displace`, `SpecularBeam`) expect values roughly centred on 0, and the
`ScalarField` adapters produce exactly that:

```csharp
ScalarField.Noise(scale: 0.15, amplitude: 1.5, driftSpeed: 0.3); // turbulence field
ScalarField.From((x, y, t) => Math.Sin(x * 0.3 + t));            // any function
// e.g. a heat-shimmer mirror without a WaveField:
ctx.Filter(Filters.Mirror(atY: 17, distortion: ScalarField.Noise(0.3, 1.2), seconds: t));
```

All of these are deterministic — the same pixel is the same every frame, so
textures never flicker. Use `Random` only for state seeded once outside the scene.

### Particles & Assemblies

Turn a picture into pixels and animate them into place — or let them go.

```csharp
var art = new BakedSurface(24, 24);                    // outside scene
art.Ensure("logo", PaintLogo);
var targets = PixelTargets.From(art.Surface, alphaThreshold: 0.4);
var targets = PixelTargets.From(24, 24, (x, y) => IsInside(x, y) ? col : (Color?)null);
var owner = PixelTargets.NearestSources(targets, landingPoints);

var assembly = new PixelAssembly(targets)
{
    Duration = 0.9,
    Spread = 11.0,
    Gravity = 10.0,
    FlightColor = Color.FromRgb(1.0, 0.85, 0.45),
    SourceOf = i => (12.0, 25.0),              // where pixel i starts
    DelayOf = i => Scatter.Value(targets[i].X, targets[i].Y) * 0.5,
    Ease = Easings.Smootherstep,
};

assembly.Draw(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);          // forms
assembly.DrawReverse(ctx, cue.LocalSeconds);   // falls apart
```

```csharp
var sparks = new ParticleField { Gravity = 14.0, Drag = 0.8 };   // outside scene

sparks.Emit(x, y, vx, vy, life, color);
sparks.Burst(12, 12, count: 26, speed: 9.0, color: Colors.Gold,
             life: 0.9, directionDegrees: -90, spreadDegrees: 360);
sparks.Step(ctx);                              // one frame at ctx.Fps
sparks.Draw(ctx, fadeOut: true, palette: Palettes.Fire, additive: true);  // additive: sparks stack to white
```

### Scene Shapes

Primitives that pixel-art scenes keep needing.

```csharp
// Tapered, shaded limb — branches, trunks, cables, smoke trails
ctx.DrawTaperedLine(x0, y0, x1, y1, halfWidth: 1.5, taper: 0.55,
                    colorLo: trunkLight, colorHi: trunkDark, shadeBias: 0.5);

// Any procedural shape with anti-aliasing: the function is asked 4x4 times per
// pixel. Return null for "not part of the shape". edgeBoost > 1 keeps interiors
// solid and only softens the outermost edge.
ctx.FillSupersampled(minX, minY, maxX, maxY, (px, py) =>
{
    var lx = ...; var ly = ...;                 // e.g. rotate around the centre
    return inside ? sailColor : (Color?)null;
}, samples: 4, edgeBoost: 1.8);

// Text in the inverse brightness of the background: dark on a bright sky,
// light on dark water — a readout that survives a scene that changes all day
ctx.DrawTextContrast(ctx.Now.ToString("HH:mm"), 4, 1, Fonts.Var4x5, alpha: 0.8);

// Voxel sprite in oblique cabinet projection, self-occluding (painter sorted).
// This is the quick 2.5D mode - fixed view, two colours per material. For a
// real camera, lighting and shadows use VoxModel + IsoCamera (see Voxel Models).
var mats = new[] { VoxelMaterial.FromBase(Colors.Sienna), VoxelMaterial.FromBase(Colors.Green) };
var model = new[] { new Voxel(0, 0, 0, 0), new Voxel(1, 0, 0, 0), new Voxel(1, 1, 0, 1) };
```
